Bond yield quotes provide important information about a bond's yield, which is the annualized return on investment for the bond. Here's how to read bond yield quotes:
* Time: This refers to the time of the quote presented and indicates when the quote was generated.
* Coupon (coupon rate): This is the amount of interest paid on the bond each period, as specified on the coupon itself. It is usually expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Price: This is the normalised price of the bond, representing the price of taking a position of $100 worth of the principal in the bond. It is often expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Yield: This is the interest rate that you would receive by buying at the current price. It is the inverse of the price and represents the annualized return on investment for the bond.
To summarize, when reading bond yield quotes, the time refers to the quote's generation time, while the coupon, price, and yield provide information about the bond's interest payments, market value, and annualized return on investment, respectively.

The different shapes of the Moon, also known as lunar phases, are determined by the amount of sunlight that is illuminating the portion of the Moon visible from Earth. This changes as the Moon orbits the Earth and the relative positions of the Moon, Earth, and Sun shift. When the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned, with the Sun and Moon on opposite sides of the Earth, we see a full moon. When the Moon is positioned between the Earth and the Sun, we see a new moon. The crescent and gibbous shapes occur during the intervals between these principal phases, when only a portion of the Moon's surface is illuminated. The specific shape at any given time depends on the Moon's position in its orbit. When a sphere is illuminated on one hemisphere and viewed from a different angle , the portion of the illuminated area that is visible will have a two - dimensional shape defined by the intersection of an ellipse and circle ( where the major axis of the ellipse coincides with a diameter of the circle ) . If the half - ellipse is convex with respect to the half - circle , then the shape will be gibbous ( bulging outwards ) whereas if the half - ellipse is concave with respect to the half - circle , then the shape will be a crescent .

The average distance from the Moon to the Earth is about 238,856 miles or 384,402 kilometers. Lunar distance (astronomy) Astronomers O'Keefe and Anderson calculated the lunar distance by observing 4 occultations from 9 locations in 1952 . They calculated a mean distance of 7008384407600000000 ♠ 384 407. 6 ± 4.7 km , however the value was refined by in 1962 by Irene Fischer , who incorporated updated geodetic data to produce a value of 7008384403700000000 ♠ 384 403. 7 ± 2 km .

There are general steps to gather the relevant worker node data: First,  Check the conditions of your worker nodes and cluster before you gather data. This includes checking the CPU and memory level of your nodes. If any node is over 80% in either CPU or memory usage, consider provisioning more nodes or reducing your workload.Secondly if all worker nodes in a cluster, or in a single zone, subnet, or VLAN are affected, you can open an initial support ticket without gathering data. However, you might later be asked to gather the relevant data. If only one or some of your worker nodes are affected, you must gather the relevant data to include in your support ticket.  Before opening a support ticket, it is recommended to review the information and follow any troubleshooting steps in Debugging worker nodes, Worker node states, and Troubleshooting worker nodes in Critical or NotReady state. To gather worker node data, you can use the command 'kubectl top node' (for Kubernetes clusters) or 'oc top node' (for OpenShift clusters), which will display the CPU and memory usage of each node and once you have gathered this information, include it in your support ticket when you open one.

An update is available for your worker nodes in a classic infrastructure cluster. As security updates and patches are put in place for the API server and other master components, you must be sure that the worker nodes remain in sync. You can make two types of updates: updating only the patch version, or updating the major.minor version with the patch version. For Classic clusters with a storage solution such as OpenShift Data Foundation you must cordon, drain, and replace each worker node sequentially. If you deployed OpenShift Data Foundation to a subset of worker nodes in your cluster, then after you replace the worker node, you must then edit the ocscluster resource to include the new worker node.You can update the master Kubernetes version with the ibmcloud ks cluster master updatecommand. Remember that your worker nodes can be only up to two versions behind the master version (n-2). The worker node IP address remains the same after the update operation.

To determine the type of update that is available, compare your current worker node versions to the latest worker node fix pack version in the Red Hat OpenShift version change log. Major updates are indicated by the first digit in the version label (4.x.x), minor updates are indicated by the second digit (x.7.x).  A major.minor update moves up the Kubernetes version of the worker node to the same version as the master. This type of update often includes changes to the Kubernetes API or other behaviors that you must prepare your cluster for. Remember that your worker nodes can only be one version behind the master version (n-1). You can update the classic worker node to the same patch by using the ibmcloud oc worker update command.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) is the network infrastructure behind virtualizing network services such as routers, firewalls, and load balancers that were traditionally run on proprietary hardware. Pre-market trading takes place before the regular trading hours (RTH) of the stock market. For example, pre-market hours are from 4:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time (ET) on the NASDAQ stock market. During pre-market hours, you can place limit orders, but you cannot place market orders due to lower liquidity. This is because the volume and liquidity are generally much lower during pre-market hours compared to RTH. If an unexpected world event occurs, the volume and liquidity might increase. It is important to note that not all brokers allow pre-market trading, and if they do, you might need to specify that you want your order to be executed during pre-market hours.

A limit order is a type of order where you set a specific price at which you want to buy or sell a security. The order will only be executed if the market price reaches the price you set. On the other hand, a market order is an order to buy or sell a security immediately at the best available current market price. Market orders do not guarantee a specific price, and the final execution price may be different from the price quoted at the time of order entry.
The choice between limit orders and market orders depends on your trading goals and risk tolerance.

Creating a single global market would be quite complex and challenging for several reasons. First, each country has its own exchange, which is closely tied to its local currency. Exchanges primarily support transactions and settlements in their local currency, and securities are denominated in a single currency. Cross-currency translation would complicate the trading process, as it would require additional steps and considerations.
Furthermore, citizens and businesses in most countries are restricted to having bank accounts in local currency, making it difficult or impossible to open a domestic bank account in a foreign-denominated currency. A public company headquartered in a given country is more likely to do business with local citizenry and businesses in that currency, and thus look for investors from the same pool, which generally means listing in local currency on an exchange in that country.

The five factors that have a major impact on your FICO credit score are:
1. Payment history: Late payments can negatively affect your score, while on-time payments can improve it.
2. Credit utilization: This refers to how much of your available credit you are currently using. Lower is better, but having 0% usage is not ideal either. Aiming for 10% or less is a good goal.
3. Credit history: This is based on the average age of all your accounts, including credit cards and loans. Older accounts are generally better for your score.
4. Credit mix: Having a diverse mix of credit types (e.g., credit cards, mortgages, auto loans) can positively impact your score.
5. New credit: Applying for new credit can result in a temporary decrease in your score due to the credit inquiries made during the application process. These inquiries remain on your report for two years.
It is important to note that errors and fraud can also impact your credit score, so regularly reviewing your credit reports from the three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion) is recommended.

The FICO score is a type of credit score developed by the Fair Isaac Corporation. It is widely used by lenders to determine the creditworthiness of potential borrowers. Credit Karma, on the other hand, provides users with free access to their credit scores, which are typically based on the VantageScore model, developed by the three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion). While FICO and VantageScore models have some similarities, they are not the same and may produce slightly different credit scores. Therefore, the credit score you see on Credit Karma might not be exactly the same as your FICO score. However, it can still provide you with a general idea of your credit standing.

Like FICO, Vantagescore is based on a proprietary formula that is not publicly available. Though there are mentions of excessively large credit card limits impacting the credit score negatively in the case of VantageScore, on the theory that the person could run up a high credit card debt quickly.

You can obtain your FICO score from the three major credit bureau (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion) via paying a nominal fee through their official website. Remember that each credit bureau may provide a slightly different FICO score, so averaging the three scores should give you a good idea of your creditworthiness. Be cautious of websites offering free credit scores, as they may not be reliable or secure for entering sensitive personal information.

Market capitalization, or Market Cap, is calculated by multiplying the share price by the number of shares. It represents the current market perception of the company's worth. On the other hand, NAV, or net asset value, is the value of the company's stock divided by the number of shares, also known as the book value. NAV reflects the value of the company's assets if it were to sell everything, pay off its debts, and shut down. While Market Cap represents current market sentiment and future expectations, NAV provides a measure of the company's tangible asset value per share. These two values often differ significantly, especially for companies expected to grow or those with substantial intangible assets. NAV is a measurable value, derived from known factors, while Market Cap is determined by the stock price, which is influenced not only by NAV but also by future expectations.

Bone marrow is found within the spongy or cancellous portions of bones. Human marrow produces approximately 500 billion blood cells per day. The main functional component of bone marrow includes the progenitor cells which are destined to mature into blood and lymphoid cells. These include white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets. In humans, the red marrow of some bones is an important site for blood cell production, in order to replace existing cells that have been destroyed by the liver.

If bone marrow does not function properly, it can lead to a decrease in the production of blood cells and blood platelets. This can be caused by various factors such as aplastic anemia, malignancies like multiple myeloma, congenital defects , autoimmune diseases, infections like tuberculosis, leukemia, or exposure to radiation or chemotherapy. Symptoms of a malfunctioning bone marrow can include fatigue, increased risk of infection, and easy bruising or bleeding. In the case of sickle cell disease, the bone marrow's attempt to compensate for the destruction of red cells is not sufficient, leading to anemia.

The treatment for sickle cell disease may include infection prevention with vaccination and antibiotics, high fluid intake, folic acid supplementation, pain medication, blood transfusion, and the medication hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea). A small percentage of people can be cured by a transplant of bone marrow cells. When treating avascular necrosis of the bone in people with sickle cell disease, the aim of treatment is to reduce or stop the pain and maintain joint mobility. Current treatment options are to rest the joint, physical therapy, pain relief medicine, joint replacement surgery, or bone grafting. High quality randomized controlled trials are needed to assess the most effective treatment option and determine if a combination of physical therapy and surgery are more effective than physical therapy alone.

A small percentage of people can be cured by a transplant of bone marrow cells. Life expectancy for people with sickle cell disease in the developed world is 40 to 60 years. About 90 % of people survive to age 20, and close to 50 % survive beyond age 50, and many people with the condition live well into adulthood with proper medical care. The disease can be life-threatening, but with appropriate treatment and management, the prognosis can be improved.

A bone marrow transplant is a potential cure for sickle cell disease, although it is difficult to obtain a suitable donor due to the specific HLA typing necessary. Ideally, a close relative would donate the bone marrow. Risks associated with the procedure are a 7% mortality rate and the possibility of graft versus host disease. In phase 1 clinical trials for adults with severe sickle cell disease, the safety and initial evidence for efficacy have been assessed, no randomized controlled trials have been reported as of 2016. It is important to note that while a bone marrow transplant can potentially cure sickle cell disease, it is not a guaranteed solution and carries significant risks.

Yes, Huntington's disease is an inherited disorder from one's parents. If a person inherits the mutated gene from an affected parent, they will typically develop the disease. The probability of inheriting the mutant allele and being affected with the disorder is 50% for each offspring of an affected individual, regardless of sex.

There is no cure for Huntington's disease. The best evidence for treatment of the movement problems is with tetrabenazine, and treatments can relieve some symptoms and in some improve quality of life. Several clinical trials of new experimental treatments are underway and planned in Huntington's disease. Carefully managed multidisciplinary caregiving becomes increasingly necessary as the disease progresses.

Yes, a number of pandemics have affected the world before COVID. The 1918 flu pandemic , which lasted until 1919, was a category 5 influenza pandemic caused by an unusually severe and deadly influenza A virus . The victims were healthy young adults , in contrast to most influenza outbreaks , which predominantly affect juvenile , elderly , or otherwise - weakened patients . Older estimates say it killed 40 -- 50 million people , while more recent research suggests that it may have killed as many as 100 million people , or 5 % of the world 's population in 1918. The third bubonic plague pandemic, also known as the modern pandemic, spread the bubonic plague disease to port cities throughout the world in the second half of the 19th century and early 20th century via shipping routes . The bubonic plague affected people in Chinatown in San Francisco from 1900 - 1904, and the people of Oakland and east bay again from 1907 - 1909. In 1994, Zimbabwe suffered outbreaks of acute diseases like plague. In 2014, West African had the Ebola virus epidemic. In 2001 the Bubonic plague affected Zambia , India , Malawi , Algeria , China , Peru , and the Democratic Republic of the Congo .   2009 saw a pandemic involving the H1N1 influenza virus (swine flu). Herpes is not generally considered a lethal disease .There are two types of herpes simplex virus , type 1 ( HSV - 1 ) and type 2 ( HSV - 2 ) . HSV - 1 more commonly causes infections around the mouth while HSV - 2 more commonly causes genital infections.Herpes is contracted through direct contact with an active lesion or body fluid of an infected person . Herpes transmission occurs between discordant partners; a person with a history of infection ( HSV seropositive ) can pass the virus to an HSV seronegative person . Herpes simplex virus type 2 is typically contracted through direct skin - to - skin contact with an infected individual , but can also be contracted by exposure to infected saliva , semen , vaginal fluid , or the fluid from herpetic blisters. However , asymptomatic carriers of the HSV - 2 virus are still contagious . In many infections , the first symptom people will have of their own infections is the horizontal transmission to a sexual partner or the vertical transmission of neonatal herpes to a newborn at term . Since most asymptomatic individuals are unaware of their infection , they are considered at high risk for spreading HSV .

Currently, there is no available vaccine  and there is no cure  for Herpes simplex virus (HSV) but Herpes simplex research has gone into vaccines for both prevention and treatment of herpes infections . Nevertheless the most effective method to avoid to get Herpes simplex  is  avoiding vaginal , oral , and anal sex . The use of condoms  decreases the risk somewhat . Daily antiviral medication taken by someone who has the infection can also reduce spread.

Vaccines can consist of live - attenuated or killed viruses , or viral proteins ( antigens ) . Live vaccines contain weakened forms of the virus , which do not cause the disease but, nonetheless , confer immunity . Such viruses are called attenuated . Live vaccines can be dangerous when given to people with a weak immunity ( who are described as immunocompromised ) , because in these people , the weakened virus can cause the original disease . Biotechnology and genetic engineering techniques are used to produce subunit vaccines . These vaccines use only the capsid proteins of the virus . Hepatitis B vaccine is an example of this type of vaccine . Subunit vaccines are safe for immunocompromised patients because they can not cause the disease.

In the first scenario, if the loan company reports the status to a credit reporting agency on behalf of both the initiating borrower and the cosigner, then both individuals get a new account on their credit report. Initially, this might decrease related credit scores slightly due to a hard pull, new account with zero history, and increased debt. However, over time, it can have a positive effect on both people's credit ratings if the loan is paid properly. Conversely, if the loan is not paid properly, it will negatively affect both people's credit. In the second scenario, if the loan company only reports to a credit agency on one of you (probably the cosigner), leaving the other as just a backup, it will have no effect on the borrower's credit. In the third scenario, if the loan company doesn't report the loan at all to a credit agency, there will be no direct impact on the borrower's credit. However, if the loan goes into collections and is reported as such, it would negatively affect the borrower's credit. Nevertheless a cosigner will make sure you are going to make every single payment on time because otherwise he will be responsible to pay it  .

Modern historians refer to the Byzantine Empire as such to distinguish it from ancient Rome. This name comes from Byzantium, the original name of Constantinople, the capital city of the empire. The citizens of the empire continued to refer to their empire as the Roman Empire or Romania and to themselves as "Romans."

During the reign of Constantine in the Byzantine Empire, Christianity was not declared the exclusive state religion, but it received special favor from the emperor, who granted it generous privileges. Constantine also established the principle that emperors could not unilaterally decide matters of religious doctrine, and instead, they should convene general ecclesiastical councils for that purpose. His summoning of the Synod of Arles and the First Council of Nicaea demonstrated his commitment to the unity of the Church and asserted his authority as its leader.The ascendancy of Christianity was briefly challenged when Emperor Julian came to power in 361 and sought to revive polytheism throughout the empire. He was later known as "Julian the Apostate" by the Church. However, Julian's efforts were reversed when he died in battle in 363.
The foundation of the Byzantine Empire was based on the belief that it was a reflection of the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth. Just as God ruled in Heaven, the Emperor, created in His image, was expected to govern on Earth and uphold His commandments. The empire aspired to be universal and aimed to encompass all the peoples of the Earth. Ideally, all people would be members of the one true Christian Church, the Orthodox Church.

Constantine I reorganized the Roman Empire in the early 4th century, around 324-337 AD. This reorganization included establishing Constantinople as the new capital and legalizing Christianity. Constantine's changes marked a significant shift that set the stage for the development of the Byzantine Empire as a distinct entity from the classical Roman Empire. Constantine moved the seat of the Empire to Constantinople, which he founded as a second Rome on the site of Byzantium, a city strategically located on the trade routes between Europe and Asia and between the Mediterranean and the Black Sea. Constantine significantly changed the Empire's military, monetary, civil, and religious institutions.

E. E. Cummings (October 14, 1894 -- September 3, 1962) was an American poet, painter, essayist, author, and playwright. Cummings wrote approximately 2900 poems, two autobiographical novels, four plays, and several essays. Many of his poems are satirical and address social issues, but they also have a strong bias towards romanticism, celebrating love, sex, and the season of rebirth. His first published work was a collection of poems titled Tulips and Chimneys (1923), which introduced the public to his characteristic eccentric use of grammar and punctuation. In addition to his poetry, Cummings also wrote children's books and novels, showcasing his versatility as a writer.

E. E. Cummings expressed a strong desire to become a poet, writing daily from the age of 8 to 22. He attended Harvard University, where he developed an interest in modern poetry while aiming for a dynamic use of language. Cummings's early work was influenced by notable modernists such as Gertrude Stein and Ezra Pound, as well as the imagist experiments of Amy Lowell. Later, his visits to Paris exposed him to Dada and surrealism, which he incorporated into his poetry. Over time, his style evolved to rely more on symbolism and allegory, but he rarely used comparisons that required objects that were not previously mentioned in the poem.

Consider seeking professional help from a credit counselor or identity theft recovery service. The FTC site provides victims with a personal recovery plan, walking through each step to take. It also provides pre-filed letters and forms to send to credit bureaus, businesses, and debt collectors.  Keep in mind that clearing their name and records can be a time-consuming and stressful process.

The MLS All-Star Game is an annual soccer game featuring select players from Major League Soccer. It originally started with a traditional East vs. West format, but later evolved into inviting a club from abroad to play against a league all-star team. Players are awarded roster spots through a combination of fan voting and selections by the appointed manager and league commissioner. The game takes place during the middle of the MLS season, which coincides with the pre-seasons of most European leagues. The MLS All-Stars have an 8-4 record in the competition as of 2015.

In the United States, it is known as soccer. Some other countries also call it soccer, but in most parts of the world, it is called football. Sports commonly called football in certain places include association football ( known as soccer in some countries ) ; gridiron football ( specifically American football or Canadian football ) ; Australian rules football ; rugby football ( either rugby league or rugby union ) ; and Gaelic football .

Yes, women's association football, also commonly known as women's football or women's soccer, is the most prominent team sport for women worldwide. In the 1970s, Italy became the first country to have professional women's football players on a part-time basis. An Italian women's football federation, known as Federazione Femminile Italiana Gioco Calcio or FFIGC, ran a "World Championships" tournament in Rome supported by the Martini and Rossi wine manufacturers, entirely without the involvement of FIFA or any of the common national associations.

The World Cup is the world's most prestigious association football tournament and has the highest television audience of any sport, making it the most popular event globally. In terms of viewership, it exceeds even the Olympic Games. On the other hand, American football is the most popular sport in the United States, with 1.1 million high school football players and nearly 70,000 college football players.

The origins of modern football codes can be traced back to Western Europe, particularly England. In 1409, King Henry IV of England made one of the earliest documented uses of the English word "football" when he issued a proclamation forbidding the levying of money for "foteball". FIFA acknowledges England as the birthplace of club football. The Football Association, established in 1863 by Ebenezer Cobb Morley, is recognized as the oldest football association, with the first set of football rules being drafted at that time.
Yes, American football evolved in the United States from the sports of association football (known in the U.S. as soccer) and rugby football.

The National Football League (NFL) has the highest average attendance of any sports league in the world, and the Super Bowl is watched by millions globally. American football is played in European countries such as Switzerland, which has American football clubs in every major city, and Germany, where the sport has around 45,000 registered amateur players. In Europe, almost all nations have their leagues, highlighting its importance, such as Austria (Austrian Football League), Germany (German Football League), Great Britain (BAFA National Leagues), France (Ligue Élite de Football Américain), and Italy (Italian Football League). However, American football has not yet reached the same level of popularity it has in, for example, North America. Football organizers are targeting Europe to expand the game.

Yes, both sports originated from the older game of rugby football in the 19th century. British colonists and the British military introduced football to North America, where it became popular in American and Canadian universities and prep schools. At that time, association football and rugby football were not as distinct as they are now, and teams would negotiate the rules before each game. It's possible to compare American football and rugby league because they share origins and similar game concepts. Along with Canadian football, the rugby league is the sport most similar to American football. Both sports involve a limited number of downs or tackles, and scoring touchdowns or tries takes precedence over goal-kicking.
The football league consists of 32 teams.

There are different ways to consider salary compensation besides the traditional gross salary. Total compensation includes salary and bonuses, as well as the cost or value of employer-paid healthcare, retirement, company cars, expense accounts, stock options, and other valuable goods or services. Additionally, the total employee cost is generally double the gross cash compensation (salary + bonuses) and includes employer-paid payroll taxes and practical costs like the cost of your computer, cubicle or office furniture, and the portion of utility costs that keep you well-lit, clean and comfortable. It's also important to consider the cost of living in the area where your employees live, as this can significantly impact the actual value of their salaries. For example, $100k in California may not go as far as $100k in other parts of the U.S. Finally, it's worth noting that salary pay does not directly translate to hourly wages, as salaried employees are compensated for a week of work, which may require more or less than 40 hours.

Yes. In many countries, employers are required to report their employee's salaries and withhold a portion for income tax, which is commonly known as "pay as you earn," "withholding taxes," or taxing "at the source." Your employer uses the W4 form in the USA to determine how much to withhold from your wages. If you leave everything at default, your salary is your only taxable income, and you only benefit from default deductions. Your employer will calculate your tax withholding based on this information. When you start a new job, your employer will typically ask you to fill out a tax form such as the W-4 Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate so they can withhold the correct federal income tax from your wages. If your employer doesn't do this, you are responsible for calculating and filing your income taxes, especially if you are self-employed, an independent contractor, or paid under the table. If your employer is reputable, they will provide you with additional information, usually in February. You must file your taxes correctly before the IRS tax deadline, generally April 15th for most people. Do I have to worry about money in my bank account? Unless you have a significant amount in your bank savings account earning interest, you won't have to pay any sort of tax on money in your bank account. If you do earn enough taxable interest, the bank will send you the proper forms to file your taxes.

In the U.S., most salaries are expressed as "gross salaries" before individual taxes are deducted. You must report all income from work, regardless of whether you save, spend, or keep it aside. This includes income from non-tax-advantaged accounts, as well as any gains or losses and dividends received. Gains and losses are realized when you actually sell, and is the difference between the price you bought for, and the price you sold for. Gains are taxed at the capital gains rate, either short-term or long-term depending on how long you owned the stock

The number of allowances you can claim is calculated by dividing your total deductions by the personal exemptions for the tax year. In 2015, the standard deduction for a married couple filing jointly is $12,600, and each person gets a personal exemption of $4,000. If your deductions exceed the standard deduction, you can subtract property taxes from your income. For example, if your income is $95,000, after taking into account the standard deduction of $12,600 and $8,000 in exemptions, your taxable income would be just under $10,000, unless you have additional undisclosed income. The most common tax credit for most people is student loan interest. If you pay $500 in student loan interest, that sum is subtracted from your tax bill.

In the United States, nearly all workers must pay Social Security and Medicare taxes, also known as payroll taxes or FICA. It's important to understand that these taxes are not savings plans, and the money you pay is not explicitly allocated to an account in your name. Instead, it funds the benefits received by current retirees and beneficiaries. When you retire, your benefits will be financed by the contributions of the still-employed workers paying these taxes. It's worth noting that FICA taxes are separate from federal and state income taxes, and as a sole proprietor, you are responsible for both types of taxes. Furthermore, there's a distinction between FICA taxes when you are an employee and when you are self-employed. Typically, FICA taxes are divided equally between the employer and the employee, with each paying half. However, if you are self-employed, you are responsible for paying both halves. This is commonly known as the self-employment tax. You may be receiving benefits, but you are also still working, so you still have to pay the tax.

No, corporations are taxed on their profits. Multinational corporations can report their earnings in any country where they operate, irrespective of where the actual sale occurs. It's difficult to pinpoint precisely where a company 'made its money.' Consequently, the US does not attempt to do so; instead, we tax them on their worldwide earnings, minus taxes paid in other countries.

If you receive dividends on an investment, those are taxed. When you exchange investments for cash, you will have to pay tax on that, disregarding capital losses, capital loss carryovers, AGI thresholds, and other special rules. For most investments, you get taxed on any gain in value in the investment or dividends paid by that investment. Usually, you don't take the tax hit until you sell the investment and realize the gain, with some exceptions for mutual funds. For bonds, CDs, and other cash-type investments, you have to pay taxes in the year they pay out the interest or dividend.
1) You can put money (up to a certain limit) in a traditional IRA and can subtract that amount from your income for tax calculation for the year you invest it. However, you are going to pay taxes on it when you take the money out at retirement. It really just delays the taxes.
2) If you put the money in a Roth IRA, you don't get a tax break now, but you don't have to pay any taxes on the money or the gains when you take it out at retirement.
3) The gains from some mutual funds can be tax exempt, but that just saves you from paying tax on the increase in value.
4) Don't fall for scams that try to use insurance policies as investments to avoid taxes. The fees are enormous, which usually makes them a rip-off.

No. Personal income tax rates and rules differ from state to state in the USA. Seven U.S. states currently don't have an income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, South Dakota, Texas, Washington, and Wyoming; some only tax income derived in the state, and some tax worldwide income (like New York or California), similarly to the Federal income taxes. However, suppose you're living abroad (i.e., you're a citizen or resident of a foreign country and live there). In that case, you're not considered a resident by most states (check with your state for specific definitions) for most, if not all, the time of your residency abroad. In such a case, you don't pay state taxes; you only pay federal taxes.  You have to remember that foreign income exclusion doesn't apply to the income from your 401k, so you pay the taxes as if you're in the US.

If you lose your job, it depends on the circumstances under which you lost your job. Unemployment insurance provides a temporary safety net to workers who lose their jobs by replacing a portion of their salary for specific periods. Each state administers its unemployment insurance program, so the rules may vary from state to state. You must have lost your job through no fault of your own to receive unemployment insurance payments. You are not eligible for unemployment insurance benefits if you quit your job or lost it because of poor performance or another justifiable reason. To receive unemployment benefits, you must be registered with an employment agency, actively seeking work, and willing to accept work should it be offered. Your payment will be a percentage of what you made in your previous job, generally between 20 percent and 50 percent, depending on your state.

Light pollution is caused by stray light from various human activities, including parking lots, sport complexes, street lights, and other sources. This scattered light makes it difficult to observe fainter stars and the Milky Way in the night sky. The larger and more developed a city is, the more light pollution it tends to produce, and the effect decreases the farther away you travel from a city.
Astronomy clubs often host public viewings and events. You can find events and other skywatching resources via the NASA Night Sky Network.

While binoculars or a telescope can enhance your skywatching experience, they are not necessary to get started. You can use your own eyes to see stars, bright planets, the Moon, comets, and shooting stars.

To safely view a solar eclipse, you will need solar viewing or "eclipse" glasses, which are much darker than regular sunglasses and block most of the Sun's light. It is also recommended to use special filters over the lenses of cameras, telescopes, or binoculars when looking at the Sun. You can also use an indirect viewing method, such as a pinhole projector, which projects an image of the Sun onto a nearby surface. It is safe to look at the Moon with unprotected eyes or through a telescope during all types and during all stages of a lunar eclipse.

To make a pinhole projector for viewing a solar eclipse, you will need two pieces of white card stock, aluminum foil, tape, and a pin, paper clip, or pencil. First, cut a 1-inch to 2-inch square or rectangular hole in the middle of one of the pieces of card stock. Tape a piece of aluminum foil over the hole. Then, flip over the paper and use your pin, paper clip, or pencil to poke a small hole in the aluminum foil. To make your projection a bit more defined, try putting the bottom piece of card stock in a shadowed area while you hold the other piece in the sunlight.

You don't need to make a pinhole projector for a lunar eclipse. Unlike a solar eclipse, it is safe to look at the Moon with unprotected eyes or through a telescope during all types and during all stages of a lunar eclipse.
It is safe to look at the Moon during a lunar eclipse because the Moon does not produce its own light, but instead reflects sunlight.

Looking directly at the Moon during a lunar eclipse is generally considered safe. The concern with solar eclipses is that looking directly at the Sun can cause serious eye damage, which is why special precautions are needed.

No, they are not the same. A mortgage is a secured debt consisting of a promissory note and a security interest that provides the mortgage holder with a secured interest in the property. A mortgage is a loan backed by a property, as specific laws cover it due to its wide usage. Therefore, the bank is not an "investor" in your house; it is simply lending you money with the property as collateral. Thus, it does not receive any share of the profit. On the other hand, refinancing, or re-fi, occurs when a debtor takes out a new loan, usually with new bank, to pay off an old one. This can be done for various reasons, primarily because the new loan terms will result in a lower monthly payment.

Ideally, a 20% down payment is suggested when buying a house. The idea behind this is that if someone can't save 1/5 of the cost of a house, they might not be responsible enough to ensure loan repayment. Additionally, by putting down 20%, you can avoid paying costly private mortgage insurance (PMI).

You can obtain various types of insurance, each with commendable rules. If you require a specific kind of insurance, the insurance company can offer it to you. Homeowners insurance helps to protect against the potential devastation of a catastrophic event, which could otherwise wipe out a large portion of our net worth. For many individuals, a fully paid-off house represents their most significant asset, often more valuable than all other savings combined. It's a risk that most people would prefer to avoid.

Renting vs. buying: There are advantages to buying, such as that instead of money going towards rent, with a mortgage, some of the payment goes towards interest, but you are also building equity. Eventually, you'll pay off the mortgage and can live rent-free. Buying with a 20% down payment can give you a strong position in the market. If you have the financial ability to assume the risk of owning, you may be better off. On the other hand, renting provides flexibility to move with minimum hassle, and the landlord assumes the risk of owning the property. Buying is sometimes better than renting, even if you're not mobile; that depends on local market conditions. If you're investing the money reasonably, you may do as well as or better than a homebuyer, and your funds will be significantly more liquid.

A home is an investment, but the value it provides isn't primarily financial. Instead, it offers consumption value as a place to live. This sets it apart from other types of investments. While you may experience some capital gains, typically in line with inflation, they are not guaranteed, and it's not easy to realize them without selling the house and moving. Essentially, there are two ways to benefit from an appreciating asset like a home: (a) Sell it and take the profit. However, if you still need a place to live, this doesn't really benefit you unless you buy a cheaper home to replace it.

Gift taxes kick in at around $14K per giver per recipient per year. That means a straight-up gift of $200K (as cash or a house) will incur a tax. Mortgage holders sign a promissory note, a promise to pay. But the contract explicitly details the penalty for nonpayment — surrender of the property. Generally, you need to be of legal age (usually 18) to apply for a loan. Also, your credit score should be good enough for the bank or loan company to feel comfortable lending you money. The reason for the age requirement is that if you're not 18, any contract you sign can be canceled (made invalid) by either you or your parents. This means that it would be legal for you to ask the bank for a $1000 loan and for the bank to provide it, if you're under 18.

The choice between a 15-year and 30-year mortgage depends on your financial situation and goals. A 15-year mortgage will typically have a lower interest rate and you'll pay off your house faster, but your monthly payments will be higher. A 30-year mortgage will have higher interest rates and you'll pay more in interest over the life of the loan, but your monthly payments will be lower. If you can afford the higher monthly payments, a 15-year mortgage may be a good choice to save money in the long run. However, if you need the lower monthly payments to afford a house, a 30-year mortgage may be a better option.

The Penobscot River originates from four branches in various lakes in north-central Maine. It specifically begins where the West Branch meets the East Branch at Medway. The river flows into the Atlantic Ocean at Penobscot Bay, and historically served as an important trade route from the Atlantic coast to interior Maine.

The West Branch is home to many types of fish, such as landlocked salmon and brook trout. There are many deep pools within the river due to the many slate ledges, making the river ideal for fishing from shore, although there are still areas that are good for canoe fishing. The West Branch is a world-class landlocked salmon river, while the East Branch is known for its smallmouth bass fishery. In 2008, the Atlantic Salmon Commission opened the main stem of the river to catch and release fly fishing for Atlantic salmon.

Yes, Main has the Androscoggin River, a 178-mile river located in the U.S. states of Maine and New Hampshire in northern New England. It joins the Kennebec River at Merrymeeting Bay in Maine before flowing into the Gulf of Maine on the Atlantic Ocean. The river is a popular fishing destination, offering opportunities to catch brook, rainbow, brown trout, landlocked salmon, and smallmouth bass.

The "best" river for fishing depends on the specific type of fish being pursued and the angler's preferences. The Yellowstone River is considered one of the world's greatest trout streams. It is officially classed as a blue ribbon stream in Montana from the park to the confluence with the Boulder River east of Livingston and from the mouth of Rosebud Creek near Rosebud, Montana, to the North Dakota border.  The Snake River was once one of the most important rivers for the spawning of anadromous fish -- which are hatched in the headwaters of rivers, live in the ocean for most of their lives, and return to the river to spawn -- in the United States.

No. The Snake River is the thirteenth longest river in the United States. The longest river is the Mississippi River, the chief river of the second-largest drainage system on the North American continent, second only to the Hudson Bay drainage system. Using the longest stream as the source, Brower's Spring in Montana, the source of the Missouri River, would give it an incredible length of 3,710 miles, making it the fourth longest river in the world after the Nile, Amazon, and Yangtze. If we use the Largest Stream measurement, the Ohio River, and by extension the Allegheny River would be the source, and the Mississippi would begin in Pennsylvania.
The Mississippi River is the chief river of the second-largest drainage system on the North American continent and is the longest river in the United States.

The Amazon River is located in the America continent, also called the Americas, and is the largest river basin in the world, covering about 40% of South America with an area of approximately 7,050,000 square kilometers (2,722,020 sq mi). It flows from west to east, starting from Iquitos in Peru and continuing across Brazil to the Atlantic. The river runs mainly through Brazil and Peru and is part of the border between Colombia and Peru. With an average discharge of about 209,000 cubic meters per second (7,400,000 cu ft/s), the Amazon represents 20% of the global riverine discharge to the ocean, greater than the combined discharge of the following seven largest independent rivers.

There are several navigable rivers in the United States. For instance, the Penobscot River becomes navigable at the city of Bangor. Additionally, both the Mississippi River and the Missouri River are commercially navigable along their entire lengths in Missouri.

Yes, the Hudson River is considered an important river in the United States. The 315-mile-long Hudson River flows through eastern New York, serving as a boundary between New Jersey and New York. The region has experienced economic revitalization, especially in green development. Notable projects such as the High Line and the Walkway Over the Hudson, along with waterfront parks and annual festivals, contribute to the area's appeal. The Hudson River valley runs primarily from north to south down the eastern edge of New York State, cutting through a series of rock types including Triassic sandstones and redbeds in the south, and much more ancient Precambrian gneiss in the north (and east).

There are several risks you might be taking if your friend puts your name down for a house he's buying.  Firstly, if you are co-signing the mortgage, the risk is that you will owe the bank the principal amount of the mortgage if your friend is unable to pay. You could come out of it a lot poorer and with your credit rating wrecked. Secondly, if you are not on the deed of the house, you would not have any legal rights to the property. This means that your friend could sell the house without your consent and you would still be responsible for the mortgage.  Thirdly, if your friend's house is a second home, he may not qualify for mortgage assistance or relief, increasing the risk for you as a co-signer.    Lastly, anyone considering this approach to talk to a lawyer and be aware of the potential tax implications.

Yes, being a veteran can help to get a mortgage. There are mortgages available specifically for veterans, such as VA loans, which offer low-to-no down payment and attractive rates. However, in a seller's market, buyers with VA loans may face challenges as some sellers might prefer offers with fewer barriers.  VA loans are not always a great deal for that matter and conventional tends to be the best including FHA. The veterans sometimes can  make themselves more appealing to sellers with non-VA loans.

FHA is an insurance policy to the bank saying that if you default they will cover a high percentage of the loan. An FHA loan has several benefits. Firstly, it only requires a 3.5% down payment and allows for lower credit scores compared to traditional mortgages. This makes it a viable option for first-time homebuyers or those with limited credit history. Secondly, the PMI costs associated with FHA loans can be reduced by the size of the down payment. However, it's important to note that FHA loans require mortgage insurance premiums (MIP) for the life of the loan, which can increase the overall cost of the mortgage.

Whether or not you need a real estate agent depends on your individual needs and circumstances. In the United States, the seller typically pays the real estate agent fee. If you don't have an agent, you may miss out on their expertise in explaining contract terms, advising you on making offers, the option to do inspections. While you can technically complete a real estate transaction without an agent, it's strongly advised to have one to guide you through the process and help you avoid potential pitfalls.

To become a real estate agent, you would typically need to take a pre-licensing course from a certified provider within your state, pass a licensing exam, and then complete a certain number of hours of post-licensing education. As for whether it pays, real estate agents typically make a commission of 3% to 3.5% of the sale price of a property, which can vary depending on the location and the sale price. However, earnings can be unpredictable and depend on various factors such as the number of transactions and the sale prices of the properties. And they only get paid if the house sells.

The decision between buying and renting a home is a complex one that depends mostly on what makes economic sense. There are three main types of clouds: public, private, and hybrid.
A public cloud consists of shared resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted in a multi-tenant environment on a virtual server and can be accessed from anywhere.
A private cloud consists of resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted on dedicated hardware, such as a bare metal server, either onsite at the company's office (or across offices) or by a cloud provider. A private cloud can be accessed from anywhere.
A hybrid cloud is a flexible solution that combines aspects of both public and private clouds. It is hosted both onsite at a company's office or across multiple offices, and by a cloud provider. This allows a hybrid cloud to be accessed from any location, making it an attractive option for many businesses.

The Deep Impact Extended Investigation (DIXI) aims to fly by comet 103P/Hartley 2 and return images and data. The Extrasolar Planet Observation and Characterization (EPOCh) investigation uses the Deep Impact imaging system to observe nearby bright stars with known large planets. This part of the mission characterizes the planets as they orbit behind and in front of the stars and searches for other planets in those systems.

The goal of the Deep Impact mission was to rendezvous with comet 9P/Tempel 1 and launch a projectile into the comet nucleus. Observations were then made of the ejecta, crater formation process, the resulting crater, and outgassing from the nucleus, particularly the newly exposed surface. The mission aimed to improve the knowledge of the physical characteristics of cometary nuclei and directly assess the interior of cometary nucleus, determine properties of the surface layers, study the relationship between the surface layers of a cometary nucleus and the possibly pristine materials of the interior, and improve our understanding of the evolution of cometary nuclei, particularly their approach to dormancy.

The Deep Impact spacecraft consists of a 370 kg cylindrical copper impactor attached to a 650 kg flyby bus. The spacecraft is a box-shaped honeycomb aluminum framework with a flat rectangular Whipple debris shield mounted on one side. There are two high- and medium-resolution instruments, each consisting of an imaging camera and an infrared spectrometer. The medium resolution camera has a field of view of 0.587 degrees and a resolution of 7 m/pixel at 700 km distance, while the high resolution camera has a field of view of 0.118 degrees and a resolution of 1.4 m/pixel at 700 km. These instruments are used to observe the ejected ice and dust from the comet nucleus.

The Deep Impact mission, launched in 2005, was designed to study comet 9P/Tempel 1. The spacecraft transferred into a heliocentric orbit and will rendezvous with comet P/Tempel 1 in July 2005.The spacecraft consisted of a flyby bus and a copper impactor, which were used to collide with the comet's nucleus and study the resulting ejecta and crater. The mission's scientific objectives included improving our understanding of the physical characteristics of cometary nuclei, determining the properties of the surface layers, studying the relationship between the surface and interior of the comet, and learning more about the evolution of cometary nuclei. After the primary mission, Deep Impact was extended to include the Deep Impact Extended Investigation (DIXI) and the Extrasolar Planet Observation and Characterization (EPOCh) investigations. DIXI involved flying by comet 103P/Hartley 2, while EPOCh used the Deep Impact imaging system to observe nearby bright stars with known large planets and search for other planets in those systems.

There are various types of dialog nodes. These include the Welcome node, which greets users when interacting with the assistant, and the Anything else node, which provides responses for unrecognized user input. You can also create custom nodes by adding a condition that triggers the assistant to process the node. It is possible to create an intent that can be recognized when a customer asks to speak to someone. After defining the intent, you can add a root-level dialog node that conditions the intent.

Intents are the purposes or goals expressed in a customer's input, such as answering a question or processing a bill payment. By recognizing the intent in a customer's input, the Watson Assistant service can choose the appropriate dialog flow to respond. Intents added from a content catalog are distinguishable from other intents by their names. Each intent name is prefixed with the content catalog name.

To create a dialogue, follow these steps:
1. Click the Dialog tab and then click Create dialog. When you open the dialog editor for the first time, the Welcome and Anything else nodes will be created for you.
2. To add more nodes, click the "More" icon on the Welcome node and select Add node below.
3. In the "If assistant recognizes" field, enter a condition that, when met, triggers your assistant to process the node. Typically, you want to add an intent as the condition.
4. Specify the condition and response for each node. The condition specifies the information that must be present in the user input for the node to be triggered, while the response is the utterance that your assistant uses to respond to the user.
5. Save your progress.
Remember, the dialogue matches intents (what users say) to responses (what the bot says back) and can ask for more details in a text response and create one or more child nodes to process the new input.

Sure, I'd be happy to explain the steps for composting at home as outlined by Madison County, NY. Step 1: Pick Out A Bin - The bin should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size. The location can affect how fast your compost dries out or holds water. A closed bin is recommended to keep critters out. If you use a closed bin, add a shovel full of soil from the ground. Keep your bin somewhere convenient to use and access. Step 2: Gather Materials - Browns are higher in carbon, and greens are higher in nitrogen. The optimal ratio is 3 parts brown to 1 part green. Avoid feces from cats and dogs, invasive plants, weed seeds, oil, fats, plastics, or non-organic matter. Gather kitchen waste in a container by your sink. Step 3: Maintain - If you have an open bin, layer some small sticks and twigs at the bottom to help with air and drainage. Layer your browns and greens, imagining you're making a bowl for your greens to lay in the middle and then adding more browns on top. Keep your compost at 40-60% water content, like a wrung out sponge. Turning helps a pile break down faster and ensures oxygen is present. Step 4: Harvest and More! - You will know when your compost is done when it has an earthy smell and looks like rich dark soil. If you do not fully turn the pile, your finished compost will be at the bottom of the pile. If you're running out of browns, shredded newspaper, paper towel, and toilet paper rolls make good brown additions. For more resources, you can check out www.compost.css.cornell.edu, www.epa.gov/recycle/composting-home, and www.dec.ny.gov/

The water that enters a storm drain like some of the heavier sediment and small objects may settle in a catchbasin , or sump , which lies immediately below the outlet , where water from the top of the catchbasin reservoir overflows into the sewer proper . Most drains have a single large exit at their point of discharge ( often covered by a grating ) into a canal , river , lake , reservoir , sea or ocean . Storm drains may discharge into man - made excavations known as recharge basins or retention ponds .

A catchbasin is a component in a storm drain system that serves as a first-line pretreatment for other treatment practices. It functions similarly to the trap in household wastewater plumbing by capturing large sediments and street litter from urban runoff before it enters the storm drainage pipes. It is designed with a single large exit at its point of discharge, often covered by a grating, and lies immediately below the outlet of the storm drain. Water from the top of the catchbasin reservoir overflows into the sewer proper, and most catchbasins are connected to a piping system that leads to a canal, river, lake, reservoir, sea, or ocean.  Unlike the plumbing trap , the catchbasin does not necessarily prevent sewer gases such as hydrogen sulfide and methane from escaping. Its performance at removing sediment and other pollutants depends on the design of the catchbasin ( for example , the size of the sump ) , and on routine maintenance to retain the storage available in the sump to capture sediment . Some  catch basins are also commonly designed with a sump area below the outlet pipe level which is a reservoir for water and debris to help prevent the pipe from clogging

There are some potential advantages and disadvantages of Immutable Object Storage:  
Advantages:  
1. Data Integrity and Long-term Data Retention: Immutable Object Storage preserves electronic records and maintains data integrity. It ensures that data is stored in a WORM (Write-Once-Read-Many), no-erasable and non-rewritable manner, which can be beneficial for industries like Financial, Healthcare, and Media content archives where data integrity is crucial. 
 2. Compliance: Immutable Object Storage can help organizations comply with certain regulations like SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511(c), and CFTC Rule 1.31(c)-(d) that govern electronic records storage and retention. When using immutable Object Storage, it is the client's responsibility to check for and ensure whether any of the feature capabilities that are discussed can be used to satisfy and comply with the key rules around electronic records storage and retention governed by the above-mentioned regulations.
Disadvantages:  
1. Limited Availability: Immutable Object Storage is available in certain regions only. Users outside these regions may not be able to use this feature. 
2. Pricing: It requires a Standard pricing plan, which could be a disadvantage for users looking for more affordable options.  
3. No High-speed Transfer: It isn't possible to use Aspera high-speed transfer with buckets with a retention policy. This could potentially slow down the data transfer process.  
4. Irreversible: Once permanent retention is enabled, it can't be reversed. Objects uploaded that use a permanent retention period cannot be deleted. This means users need to be sure about their need to permanently store objects. 
5. Legal Holds: The retention policy is enforced until the end of a retention period and the removal of any legal holds. This could potentially cause issues if there are legal disputes or investigations. Please note that the actual advantages and disadvantages may vary depending on the specific use case and requirements.

The Great Wall of China was built using various materials over different periods. Originally, it was mainly constructed from rammed earth, stones, and wood. During the Ming Dynasty (1368--1644), bricks became heavily used, along with materials such as tiles, lime, and stone. The bricks were easier to work with, could bear more weight, and endured better than rammed earth.

The frontier walls built by different dynasties have multiple courses. Collectively, they stretch from Dandong in the east to Lop Lake in the west, from present - day Sino - Russian border in the north to Qinghai in the south. The walls built by the Ming dynasty measure 8,850 km. Faced with the threat of the Göktürks from the north, the Qi built up to 3,000 li about 1,600 kilometers. The Xuan - Da portion of the Great Wall totaled about 850 kilometers of wall, with some sections being doubled - up with two lines of wall, some tripled or even quadrupled. Chancellor Wanyan Xiang convinced the emperor to build an extensive systems of walls, which consisted of a 700 kilometers outer wall from Heilongjiang to Mongolia and a 1,000 kilometers network of inner walls, north and northeast of Beijing. Together, they formed a roughly elliptical web of fortifications 1,400 kilometers in length.

Many scholars have operated under the belief that the Great Wall continually defended China 's border against the raids and invasions of the various nomadic groups of the Eurasian Steppe with an eye to expansion. Towards the end of the Ming, the Great Wall helped defend the empire against the Manchu invasions that began around 1600. The usefulness of the Great Wall as a defense line against northern nomads became questionable under the Qing dynasty, since China proper, Manchuria, and Mongolia were all under Qing control. So instead, the Great Wall became the means to limit Han Chinese movement into the steppes. Rather than being defensive, the walls indicate the northward expansions of the three northern states and their desire to safeguard their recent territorial acquisitions.

In 221 BC , the state of Qin completed its conquest over the other Warring States and united China under Qin Shi Huang , the first emperor of China. Intending to impose centralized rule and prevent the resurgence of feudal lords , he ordered the destruction of the sections of the walls that divided his empire. Contrary to the building of the outer walls, which were built to stabilize the newly united China, the inner walls threatened the unity of the empire. In the north, the state of Wei and the Yiqu built walls to protect themselves from Qin aggression, but were still unable to stop Qin from eating into their territories. The settlement of the north continued up to Qin Shi Huang 's death in 210 BC.

Meng Tian was a Chinese general and politician who served under Emperor Qin Shi Huang during the Qin Dynasty. He is best known for leading the northern expedition against the Xiongnu people. Meng Tian was responsible for building and extending the Great Wall of China along the empire's northern border. Meng Tian introduced 30,000 settler families to colonize the newly conquered territories. When Meng Tian's settlements in the north were abandoned, the Xiongnu nomads moved back into the Ordos Loop as the Qin empire became consumed by widespread rebellion. Upon Qin Shi Huang's death in 210 BC, Meng Tian was ordered to commit suicide in a succession conspiracy.

When China opened its borders to foreign merchants and visitors after its defeat in the First and Second Opium Wars, the Great Wall became a main attraction for tourists. The sections of the Great Wall around Beijing municipality are especially famous: they were frequently renovated and are regularly visited by tourists today. In 1952, the scholar - turned - bureaucrat Guo Moruo laid out the first modern proposal to repair the Great Wall. Five years later, the renovated Badaling became the first section to be opened to the public since the establishment of the PRC. The Badaling Great Wall has since become a staple stop for foreign dignitaries.

The Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA) is a United States federal law that defines and protects the institution of marriage. enacted in 1996. It was introduced by Georgia Representative Bob Barr and Senator Don Nickles of Oklahoma. The Act was intended by Congress to reflect and honor a collective moral judgment and to express moral disapproval of homosexuality. It also defined marriage for federal purposes as the legal union of a man and a woman as husband and wife, and a spouse as a husband or wife of the opposite sex. Section 3 of DOMA defines marriage and spouse for federal purposes. Section 3 codified non-recognition of same - sex marriages for all federal purposes, including insurance benefits for government employees, social security survivors ' benefits, immigration, bankruptcy, and the filing of joint tax returns, as well as excluding same - sex spouses from the scope of laws protecting families of federal officers, laws evaluating financial aid eligibility, and federal ethics laws applicable to opposite - sex spouses.

In determining the meaning of any Act of Congress , or of any ruling , regulation , or interpretation of the various administrative bureaus and agencies of the United States , the word ' marriage ' means only a legal union between one man and one woman as husband and wife. Additionally, any other State , territory , possession , or tribe respecting a relationship between persons of the same sex that is treated as a marriage under the laws of such other State , territory , possession , or tribe , or a right or claim arising from such relationship based on "Defense of Marriage Act,".

The typical wedding involves a couple proclaiming their commitment to one another in front of their close relatives and friends , often presided over by a religious figure such as a minister , priest , or rabbi , depending upon the faith of the couple . Secular weddings are also common , often presided over by a judge , Justice of the Peace , or other municipal official . At a wedding reception , the father of the bride , in his role as host , regularly offers the first toast , thanking the guests for attending , offering tasteful remembrances of the bride 's childhood , and wishing the newlyweds a happy life together . The best man usually proposes a toast in the form of best wishes and congratulations to the newlyweds . A best man 's toast takes the form of a short speech ( 3 -- 5 minutes ) that combines a mixture of humor and sincerity . The actual `` toast '' is then delivered at the end of the speech and is a short phrase wishing the newlyweds a happy , healthy , loving life together . The maid of honor may follow suit , appropriately tailoring her comments to the bride . The groom may offer the final toast , thanking the bride 's parents for hosting the wedding , the wedding party for their participation , and finally dedicating the toast to the bridesmaids .

The primary reason is that joy must always be tempered . Choosing and investing in only one stock is risky. You can lower your risk by diversifying, or investing in lots of different stocks. An ETF is an ""Exchange Traded Fund"". It trades like a stock, on the stock market. Basically by buying one ETF, you can have ownership in the underlying companies that make up the ETF. An ETF does not track any one individual stock. It is a marketable security that tracks an index, a commodity, bonds, or a basket of assets like an index fund. ETFs can be a cost-effective way to gain exposure to a broad portfolio of investments. Like mutual funds, ETFs can offer diversification, which can help spread risk. However, unlike mutual funds, ETFs have a higher liquidity and they can be traded at any time during the trading hours.

It is recommended to have at least $5000 to invest in stocks or ETFs to minimize the impact of commissions. If you have a smaller amount to invest, you might consider a Vanguard mutual fund, which will not charge commissions and will have annual expenses only slightly higher than the corresponding ETF.

A 401K (pre-tax or Roth) account or an IRA (Deductible or Roth) account is a retirement account. Traditional IRA and 401(k) accounts allow you to make pre-tax contributions, giving you an immediate tax deduction when you contribute. Roth IRA, Roth 401(k) are funded with after tax money.  Choosing between an IRA and a 401K depends on your personal circumstances and preferences. Here are some key points to consider: * A 401K is typically offered by your employer, while an IRA is an individual retirement account that you set up for yourself. * A 401K may have more limited investment options compared to an IRA, but it may also offer matching contributions from your employer, a free money to you.  * If you expect to be in a lower tax bracket in retirement than you are now, a traditional IRA or 401K may be a better choice, as it allows you to defer taxes until retirement. It's a good idea to start with the 401K offered by your company, especially if they have matching funds. Ultimately, the best choice for you will depend on your individual circumstances, so it's a good idea to consult with a financial advisor or do further research to determine the best option for you.

Before dental and medical procedures or examinations, alert health care providers about your allergy. Ask to be scheduled as the first patient in the morning to minimize your exposure to airborne latex particles. Participate in educational and training programs regarding latex allergy. If the allergy sufferer is a child, alert school and/or day care providers. Work with your allergist, local hospital and medical facilities to find latex-safe environments where you can go for treatment. Contact your local emergency responders (police, fire and ambulance service) to inform them of your condition so a plan of care can be developed before there is an actual emergency. Health care facilities are beginning to create latex-safe treatment areas and surgical suites to accommodate people who are allergic to latex. Check with your local hospital.

Vulnerability Advisor scans images that are stored in IBM Cloud Container Registry to find potential security vulnerabilities in the image content. It checks for known software vulnerabilities and weak system configurations. Also, it detects security issues and potential vulnerabilities. When it finds any issues, it provides suggestions to help fix the reported vulnerabilities.

Vulnerability Advisor v4 is now available, and you should update Vulnerability Advisor to version 4 by 19 June 2023. If you use one of the Vulnerability Advisor version 3 SDKs to access Vulnerability Advisor, you must update to the Vulnerability Advisor version 4 SDK.
About how to update to version 4, see Update Vulnerability Advisor to version 4 by 19 June 2023.

Vulnerability Advisor version 4 uses new architecture and a different scanning engine compared to version 3. In version 4, the image is indexed the first time it is pushed and the vulnerability assessment is calculated every time Vulnerability Advisor is queried about that image. In contrast, version 3 triggers the scanning of an image when a new image is pushed to the registry, when a new security notice is released for a package that is installed in the image, or while an image is tagged in the registry. Additionally, version 3 is deprecated from 19 June 2023 and it is recommended to update to version 4.

You can protect the confidentiality of your IBM Cloud® Container Registry images, and ensure that hosts that aren't trusted can't run the images. You can create an encrypted image by using an RSA public-private key pair to encrypt and decrypt the image. The public key is used to encrypt the image, while a private key is a secret and then build a container image by using a Dockerfile, and only users that have that private key can use it to decrypt the image.

Yes, of course! IBM Cloud® Container Registry is integrated with the Security and Compliance Center to help you manage security and compliance for your organization. It provides a multi-tenant, highly available, scalable, and encrypted private image registry. It allows you to store and access your private container images, and it is hosted and managed by IBM. You can use Container Registry by setting up your own image namespace and pushing container images to your namespace. This service is required if you are using Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud.

To set up namespaces in IBM Cloud Container Registry, you can follow these steps: 1. Choose a unique namespace name that meets the requirements (4-30 characters, starts and ends with a letter or number, contains lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only). Avoid putting personal information in your namespace names. 2. Run the `ibmcloud cr namespace-add` command followed by your desired namespace name to create a new namespace. 3. Verify the creation of the new namespace by running the `ibmcloud cr namespace-list` command. Remember that you can have up to 100 namespaces in each region, and if you're unsure whether a namespace is already set for your account, you can run the `ibmcloud cr namespace-list` command with the `-v` option to retrieve existing namespace information.

To update the cluster master, you should follow these steps:
1. Check if your cluster is unsupported by reviewing the State field in the output of the `ibmcloud ks cluster ls` command or in the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service console.
2. If your cluster is unsupported, you need to create a new cluster and deploy your apps to the new cluster. Then, you can delete the unsupported cluster.
3. Before updating to the latest version, make sure to update deprecated clusters to a supported version that is one or two behind the current version. For example, you can update to version 1.21 or 1.22 before updating to the latest version, 1.23.
4. If the worker nodes run a version two or more behind the master, update them to the same version as the master to avoid issues with your pods.
5. Finally, update the cluster using the instructions provided in the IBM Cloud documentation: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/containers?topic=containers-updateupdate>.
Keep in mind that updating a cluster to a new version may impact deployed apps, so it's essential to prepare accordingly.

The CIS Kubernetes Benchmark is a framework of specific steps to configure Kubernetes more securely and with standards that are commensurate to various industry regulations. It is published by the Center for Internet Security (CIS). When a new Kubernetes version is released, IBM engineers compare the default configuration of a cluster that runs that Kubernetes version against the benchmark and publishes the results in the IBM Cloud documentation. The benchmark recommendations are provided by the Center for Internet Security, and it covers recommendations for master components, etcd, control plane configurations, worker nodes, and policies such as for users, network, and pod security.

No, you can deploy IBM Cloud® Kubernetes Service clusters worldwide, not just in the USA. Cloud Kubernetes Service is available in a subset of these locations, including worldwide multizone regions and single zone regions.

Here are some best practices for using IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service: 1. Keep your cluster up-to-date: Regularly update your cluster to avoid getting into an unsupported state and experiencing operational impact. 2. Ensure compatibility between master and worker nodes: Your worker nodes can't run a later major.minor Kubernetes version than the master. They can be up to two versions behind the master version (n-2). 3. Update worker nodes for each patch version: Unlike the master, you must update your workers for each patch version. 4. Review the version archive instructions: If your cluster runs an unsupported Kubernetes version, follow the version archive instructions.

You can not compare dynamic and static secrets in terms of one being "better" than another. There are differences between them. Dynamic secrets have their expiration date and time enforced when their secret data is read or accessed, while static secrets have their expiration date and time enforced at secret creation or rotation time. With a Secrets Manager, you can create, lease, and centrally manage secrets that are used in IBM Cloud services or your custom-built applications.

Both dynamic and static secrets have their own ways of protecting against vulnerabilities. The static code scan stage runs a static code analyzer tool on the specified app repo codebases.  The Dynamic scan stage runs a dynamic application security testing tool to find vulnerabilities in the deployed application.

Both dynamic and static secrets can have their expiration dates enforced, leading to the rotation of the secrets. The key difference lies in when this enforcement occurs. For static secrets, the expiration date and time are enforced at secret creation or rotation time. In contrast, for dynamic secrets, the expiration date and time are enforced when the secret data is read or accessed. When trying to rotate a secret, the request's success depends on whether the previous version is locked or not. Automatic rotation is available only for secrets that are generated by Secrets Manager. With IBM Cloud® Secrets Manager, you can design a strategy for rotating your secrets and sensitive data.
