In the U.S., salaries are generally expressed as gross salaries, which do not include taxes, benefits, or additional employer-paid expenses like equipment and office space. These employer expenses can effectively double the total employee cost. It's important to note that a salary is not directly comparable to an hourly wage, as it reflects payment for a week's work rather than specific hours. Living costs vary across the U.S., so $100k in California does not provide the same standard of living as the same amount in other states with lower costs of living. Different salary structures for employees include performance-based bonuses, profit-sharing, and stock options.

Many countries have employers report their employee's salaries and withhold some money for income tax purposes. This is often called "pay as you earn" or "withholding taxes". The system is typically designed to encourage workers to pay their taxes based on their income throughout the year instead of in a single payment. The amount withheld depends on the employee's salary, personal income tax information, and exemptions, and is reported to the relevant tax authorities. Often, taxpayers can receive a refund if they pay more in income tax than they owe. However, it is important to note that the tax system can vary by country, and specific regulations may apply. If an individual has other income or deductible expenses, they may need to file a separate tax return or report additional information. It is always recommended to check the regulations in the specific country in question.

Income tax is a tax imposed by governments on individuals or entities (taxpayers) who earn income as a way to raise revenue for public services and programs. The tax is based on the taxpayer's total amount of income, which includes wages, salaries, commissions, rental income, dividends, and capital gains. Income taxes are used to fund the operations of the government, such as building and maintaining infrastructure, providing education and healthcare, funding defense and national security, and more. Taxes are a crucial way to ensure the government can provide for its citizens and maintain an orderly society. In the US, the federal government imposes an income tax on individuals and corporations, and so do many state and local governments. The tax rate varies based on the amount of income earned and the taxpayer's filing status. The IRS requires all citizens and residents to file a federal income tax return each year, reporting all income received and expenses related to earning that income. Those who owe taxes after accounting for credits, deductions, and exemptions must file a tax return and pay any difference before the federal income tax deadline, usually April 15.

There are many deductions that can lower your taxable income. For example, as a married couple filing jointly, you can subtract $12,600 as a standard deduction, plus $8,000 in exemptions, for a total of $20,600 off the top, leaving you with $10,000 taxable unless you have other income not disclosed. If your deductions are higher than the standard deduction, you will be able to subtract property taxes from your income. Some other common deductions include student loan interest, contributions to a traditional IRA, and donations to qualified charities. You can itemize deductions, but in most cases, if your total deductions don't exceed your standard deduction, you should take the standard deduction. The IRS also offers special deductions for certain types of income, such as self-employment income, rental income, and investment income. It's important to keep track of your income and expenses so you can take advantage of all the deductions you are entitled to.

FICA, or the Federal Insurance Contributions Act, is the set of rules that define how much you and your employer must pay towards Social Security and Medicare. When it comes to FICA taxes, you owe both self-employment (SE) taxes and wage taxes. These taxes are for Medicare and Social Security (together they are known as FICA taxes). Social Security is the largest expenditure in the federal budget and provides money to people who are unable to work due to age or disability. The taxes are paid in, and the benefits are paid out on the basis of individual work histories. The money is used to pay benefits to current retirees, not saved for your own future. Medicare is the same idea but covers elderly healthcare expenses. While the federal government levies these taxes, it only funds Medicare, while Social Security is funded separately from the general fund. SE taxes apply to roughly 92.35% of every dollar that you make, with the remaining 7.65% being withheld as wage taxes by your employer. The SE tax rate is 15.3%, but you get to take a deduction on half of this, so the effective rate is 14.13%. Note that your employer's contribution is not technically a deduction, but rather an addition to your salary that is considered taxable income.

No, personal income tax and corporate tax are two different types of tax systems. While both systems aim to collect revenue for the government, the methodology and tax rates can vary significantly.

1. Personal Income Tax: This is levied on an individual's earnings, including wages, salaries, dividends, interest, and any other form of income. Individuals typically file annual tax returns to report their income and determine their tax liability. In many jurisdictions, personal income tax rates are progressive, meaning that as a person's income increases, they are subject to higher tax rates.
2. Corporate Tax: This is the tax that companies and corporations are required to pay on their profits. The tax amount is generally determined by subtracting deductible expenses (such as salaries, rent, utilities, or depreciation) from a company's gross revenue. The remaining amount, known as taxable income, is then taxed according to the corporate tax rates set by the tax authority. In some jurisdictions, corporate tax rates are also structured progressively, with higher-earning corporations subject to higher tax rates.

While it may seem intuitive to compare personal income tax and corporate tax, it's essential to understand that they serve two distinct purposes. Personal income tax is levied on an individual's earnings, while corporate tax targets company profits. In addition, the tax rates, tax credits, and deductions available to individuals and corporations can vary widely depending on the country, state, or region's specific tax code. Moreover, certain countries tax both corporations and individuals on the same income, leading to double taxation. In such cases, corporations may be granted deductions, credits, or other incentives to offset the double taxation impact.

In most cases, investments are taxed on any gain in value or dividends paid by the investment. Exemptions include certain mutual funds that provide tax-exempt gains. However, most individual investments do not experience a tax hit until the investment is sold, and the gains are realized. This is known as capital gains tax. The rate varies, depending on the type of investment and the length of time the investment has been held. Conversely, certain cash-type investments like bonds and CDs result in taxes in the year they pay out interest or dividends. The gains from dividends are reported on Schedule B of the tax return. This schedule also reports ordinary dividends received from securities and mutual funds during the year. If you have a significant income from dividends or capital gains, the IRS requires you to make quarterly estimated payments. These payments are made on estimated income received during the quarter, including wages, dividends, and capital gains. The estimated taxes for the first three quarters of the year are paid on IRS Form 1040 ES. The fourth quarter payment is typically due on January 15 of the following year, and all payments are credited towards the annual tax liability. However, the process can be complex, and many taxpayers find that they overestimate or underestimate their payments, which can result in fines and penalties for underpayment.

In the United States, state and local tax systems may vary, with some states having no state income tax at all. If you have an income source in a state that doesn't tax that source of income, and you live in a state that does, you may be required to report the gross income and claim an exclusion or deduction for that income. For example, a Nevada resident who works remotely in San Francisco may have to pay California income tax even though they don't live there, since their income was earned there. Additionally, in states with progressive income tax rates, the tax rate increases as taxable income increases. Some states offer tax incentives to promote renewable energy or other environmentally friendly investments. These incentives can take the form of tax credits, tax deductions, or tax exemptions. For example, a state may offer a tax credit for the purchase of a hybrid or electric vehicle.

If you lose your job, you may be eligible for unemployment insurance benefits, also known as unemployment compensation or unemployment benefits. Unemployment insurance provides a temporary safety net to workers who lose their jobs by replacing a portion of their salary for certain periods. Each state administers its own unemployment insurance program so some rules may vary from state to state. To receive unemployment insurance payments, you must have lost your job through no fault of your own. If you quit your job or lost it because of poor performance or another justifiable reason, you are not eligible for unemployment insurance benefits. State unemployment insurance programs require claimants to have worked sufficiently before they can claim benefits. Before you begin receiving benefits, you must complete a waiting period of typically one or two weeks. If you find a new job during this period, you will not be eligible for unemployment benefits, even if the job does not pay you as much as your previous job. After the waiting period, you will begin to receive your weekly payments. The payment you receive will be a percentage of what you made in your previous job, generally between 20 percent and 50 percent, depending on your state. Employers pay for unemployment insurance through payroll taxes. So, while employees' work and earnings history are important to funding their unemployment benefits, the money does not come from their pay. Employer unemployment insurance contributions depend on several factors, including how many former employees have received benefits.

Light pollution affecting skywatching primarily comes from stray light from parking lots, sport complexes, street lights, and other human activities. This scattered light is combined and manifests as a glow in the night sky, making it difficult to observe fainter stars and the Milky Way. The larger and more developed a city is, the more light pollution it tends to produce. To minimize the impact of light pollution, it's recommended to head to less developed areas away from town.

If you're interested in skywatching, you can enjoy free viewing of celestial events, such as meteor showers, lunar eclipses, and the International Space Station passing overhead. To make the most of your skywatching experience, find a location away from city lights and give your eyes about 20 minutes to adjust to the darkness. Also, check out resources like NASA's "What's Up" monthly skywatching highlights video and the Night Sky Network for more information about local astronomy clubs and events.

In terms of health effects, research suggests that light pollution can cause disruptive sleep patterns, which in turn can lead to adverse health effects. The main issue is that artificial light at night can suppress the production of the hormone melatonin, which our bodies use to regulate sleep. However, this effect is not specific to skywatching activities.

The number one priority when seeking an excellent location for skywatching is to get away from bright city lights. Wide open areas without lots of tall trees or mountains nearby make for good viewing spots, since you can see more of the sky. Examples include places like a large field, a wide valley, and the shore of a lake or the ocean. Any location you select should be a place where you can feel safe at night. If you have access to binoculars or a telescope, they will extend your vision and enhance the experience – but they are by no means necessary to get started.

To safely view a solar eclipse, you will need special solar viewing or eclipse glasses. These glasses are much darker than normal sunglasses and block most of the Sun's light. Looking directly at the Sun without eclipse glasses can damage your eyes. Special filters are also needed to cover the lenses of cameras, telescopes, or binoculars. The only time during a solar eclipse when it’s safe to look at the Sun without eclipse glasses is during the brief total phase of a total solar eclipse, when the Moon completely blocks the Sun’s bright face. Ask an adult for help looking at the Sun.

To make a simple pinhole projector, you will need two white sheets of paper, scissors, aluminum foil, and tape.

1. Cut a small square or rectangle in the middle of one piece of paper.
2. Tape a piece of aluminum foil over the hole.
3. Use a pin, paper clip, or pencil to poke a small hole in the aluminum foil.
4. Hold the piece of paper with the aluminum foil hole above the second sheet of paper, with the foil facing the Sun.

You will see an image of the Sun projected onto the second piece of paper. The farther away you hold the projector, the bigger the projected image will be. To make your projection a bit more defined, you can put the bottom piece of paper in a shadowed area while you hold the other piece in the sunlight.

You don't need any special equipment to view a lunar eclipse! In fact, it's safe to look at a lunar eclipse with your naked eyes. You can also use binoculars or a telescope to get a closer look. If you want to take pictures of a lunar eclipse, you can use a camera with a telephoto lens or a telescope and a camera adapter. You can also use smartphones with certain types of telescope mounts.

It is safe to look at the Moon with unprotected eyes during all types and during all stages of a lunar eclipse because the Moon does not shine its own light. It reflects the light of the Sun. During a lunar eclipse, the Moon passes into Earth's shadow and the surface appears red or other Earth-shadows colors. Because the intensity of the light is so much lower, it is safe to view with unprotected eyes. In contrast, during a solar eclipse, the Sun appears much brighter than the Moon does, and it can be dangerous to look directly at the Sun without special eye protection.

If you are still nervous about viewing the lunar eclipse without eye protection, you can use the same solar viewing glasses that you would use to protect your eyes during a solar eclipse. However, this is not necessary, as it is safe to view a lunar eclipse with unprotected eyes.

According to the provided documents, refinancing and getting a mortgage are not the same thing, but they are related. A refinancing, or re-fi, is when a debtor takes out a new loan for the express purpose of paying off an older one, usually to lower monthly payments. Debt consolidation is a form of refinancing. Refinancing is most commonly heard in reference to refinancing a home mortgage. In a refinancing, a new bank pays off the outstanding debt, leaving the net amount of outstanding debt roughly equal. However, a refinancing can be difficult for a homeowner to get, especially if the homeowner owes more than the home's worth or is not creditworthy. Mortgage, on the other hand, is a (secured) debt, where a bank lends you money with the property as collateral, but it is not an investment in the property. In both cases, the bank is not a co-owner of the property, but in a mortgage a bank lends you money to buy a property, while in a refinance a bank pays off the outstanding debt.

In economics, the term value generally refers to the significance, worth, or usefulness of something. In classical and neoclassical economics, the price of an item is determined by the demand and supply for that item and is assumed to represent its value. However, in heterodox economic thought and in some branches of Marxist analysis, the value is treated as a separate concept that is not always equivalent to price. It may refer to:

* Intrinsic value, the value of something that is not dependent on the market or the perception of a group of people
* Use value, the value or usefulness of something
* Economic value, the value as seen from the perspective of economics
* Commercial value, the value to business or commerce
* Subjective value, the value as perceived by a perceiving subject
* Surplus value, the value created by worker above the remuneration of worker or labor cost
* Labor theory of value, a theory of value that argues that the economic value of a good or service is determined by the total amount of socially necessary labor required to produce it.
Moreover, the value of an asset is usually measured by its expected earnings.

This could refer to different things depending on the context in which the term is used. It could refer to the monetary value of an item, the value it holds for the owner, or the value it has for society as a whole. The value of an item can also change over time depending on various factors such as supply and demand, inflation, and market trends. In accounting, business, and investing, it is important to determine the value of an asset to make informed decisions.

Additionally, the value of money can change over time due to inflation and deflation. It is important to understand the true worth of your assets and their current value, as this can impact your financial decisions and future financial stability.

However, it's worth noting that the value of something can be subjective and can vary from person to person. The same item can have different values to different people depending on their needs and preferences.

The tax treatment of gifts depends on the relationship between the giver and the recipient and the size of the gift. Generally, in the US, the first $15,000 (for 2020 and 2021) of any gift by a giver to a recipient during a calendar year are considered non-taxable. If the gift is larger, then the giver must file a gift tax return, but unless they have given more than $11.58 million (for 2020) or $11.7 million (for 2021) during their lifetime, they won't actually owe any tax. For tax purposes, a gift is any transfer to an individual, either directly or indirectly, where full consideration (measured in money or money's worth) is not received in return. A gift does not include amounts paid for tuition or medical services paid directly to the institution or caregiver. While the gift tax provisions apply to each transfer made by a donor, a transfer to a spouse is generally tax-free. However, special provisions apply to split gifts between spouses.

The article suggests that if a borrower does not pay the mortgage, the penalty is the surrender of the property. The borrower is not escaping the consequences of default but rather suffering them. By not paying the mortgage, the borrower forfeits their rights to the property. This is a straightforward and explicit provision in the mortgage contract. The borrower is not getting away scot-free but is instead subjecting themselves to the consequences of their default. Ultimately, the lender will repossess the property and sell it off in order to recoup their losses. The borrower will still be responsible for any outstanding debt that remains after the sale of the property.

The minimum age for taking out a loan is generally 18. At this age, you are considered to have reached the age of majority and can enter into binding contracts. However, aside from age, other factors are considered when applying for a mortgage, such as income, credit score, and having enough savings. Lenders want to ensure that you have the means to repay before they approve your application.

In deciding between a 15-year and a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, it's important to consider your financial situation and goals. Given that a 30-year mortgage will typically have a lower monthly payment and a 15-year mortgage will carry a lower interest rate, it may seem like a no-brainer that the 15-year mortgage is the better option. However, the choice is not always clear-cut. If you can afford the higher monthly payment that comes with a 15-year mortgage and have the flexibility to continue to meet other financial goals, a 15-year mortgage may be the better option. However, if you need a lower monthly payment to meet other financial goals or to feel comfortable with the loan, a 30-year mortgage may be the better option. The Penobscot River starts from four branches in several lakes in north-central Maine. The West Branch and East Branch unite at Medway. The river then flows 109 miles south, past Bangor, where it becomes navigable, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean in Penobscot Bay.

The West Branch of the Penobscot River originates from the Ripogenus Dam near Chesuncook Lake. It's known for its deep pools and heavy rapids, making it ideal for fishing, especially for landlocked salmon and brook trout. There are also campsites available for visitors looking to stay for more than one day. The West Branch eventually joins the East Branch at Medway to form the main stem of the Penobscot River, which then proceeds to flow into the Atlantic Ocean.

Yes, the Kennebec River is an important river system in Maine, with a drainage basin of approximately 17,000 square kilometers and a length of approximately 240 kilometers. The river originates from Moosehead Lake and flows southeast past several towns, including Waterville and Augusta. The lower Kennebec has been designated as a National Recreation Trail and is popular for whitewater rafting and kayaking. The river's estuary, Merrymeeting Bay, is a rich ecosystem that supports diverse wildlife, including waterfowl, bald eagles and several species of fish.

While the Penobscot River is one of the most renowned fishing rivers in the United States, it is difficult to definitively declare it the "best" river for fishing in the entire country. The quality of a river for fishing can vary greatly depending on the time of year and the specific type of fish being sought. However, the Penobscot River does offer a diverse range of fish species and world-class fishing opportunities, making it an excellent choice for those looking to enjoy some quality fishing in a breathtaking natural setting.

The Mississippi River is the longest river in the United States, while the Snake River is the thirteenth longest. The Mississippi's total length is approximately 2,320 miles (3,730 km), depending on whether the measurements are made from its traditional source at Lake Itasca or from Brower's Spring in Montana, the source of the Missouri River. Using the latter measurement, it has a length of 3,710 miles. The Snake River, on the other hand, has a length of 1,078 miles (1,735 km). The Snake River's watershed is the 10th largest among North American rivers, and covers almost 108,000 square miles (280,000 km) in portions of six U.S. states: Wyoming, Idaho, Nevada, Utah, Oregon, and Washington, with the largest portion in Idaho. Most of the Snake River watershed lies between the Rocky Mountains on the east and the Columbia Plateau on the northwest. The Snake River is a major tributary of the Columbia River, and its average discharge at the mouth constitutes 31% of the Columbia's flow at that point. Above the confluence, the Snake River is slightly longer than the Columbia, but its drainage basin is slightly larger.

In terms of length, the longest river in the United States is the Missouri River, with a length of 3,767 km (2,341 miles) if we consider the official government-endorsed measurement to the Brower's Spring in Montana. However, if we consider the largest stream measurement, some consider the Mississippi River to be the longest because it has the largest water discharge, even though it is technically shorter than the Missouri River.

In terms of drainage area, the Mississippi River is the second-largest drainage system in North America, second only to the Hudson Bay drainage system. The Mississippi River basin covers an area of 3,220,000 sq km (1,240,000 sq mi) and receives water from 31 U.S. states and two Canadian provinces.

In terms of water discharge, the Mississippi River is the largest and discharges an average of 17,000 cubic meters per second (600,000 cubic feet per second) at its mouth. However, it is important to note that the discharge rate can vary significantly throughout the year, especially during spring floods.

So, depending on the criteria used, the largest river in the United States can be the Missouri River, the Mississippi River, or, technically, neither.

Several rivers in the USA are navigable, including:

1. Mississippi River: flows from northern Minnesota, down through the states of Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Louisiana before empting into the Gulf of Mexico.
2. Missouri River: the longest river in North America, flowing from the Rocky Mountains down through Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Iowa, and Missouri before joining the Mississippi River in St. Louis.
3. Ohio River: flows from western Pennsylvania, through Ohio and Indiana, along the borders of West Virginia and Kentucky, and eventually meets the Mississippi River in Illinois.
4. Hudson River: runs from the Adirondack Mountains to Hudson Bay in New York, flowing south through Troy and Albany before emptying into New York Harbor.
5. Tennessee River: a tributary of the Ohio River that flows from Tennessee, through Alabama, Kentucky, and Mississippi, before joining the Ohio River.
6. Columbia River: flows from the Rocky Mountains in British Columbia, Canada, down through Washington and Oregon before emptying into the Pacific Ocean.
7. Rio Grande: the fourth longest river system in the United States, flowing west and south from the San Juan Mountains of Colorado, through New Mexico and Texas, before forming part of the US-Mexico border.
8. Colorado River: flows through parts of the states of Colorado, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, and California before emptying into the Gulf of California.
9. St. Johns River: the longest river in the state of Florida, flows north from Indian River County, through the cities of Palm Bay, Melbourne, Titusville, and Jacksonville, before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean.
10. Yukon River: the fifth longest river in the United States, flowing from the Coast Mountains in British Columbia, Canada, through Alaska and into the Bering Sea.

Yes, the Hudson River has had an impactful and distinct history since its discovery in 1609 by Henry Hudson. Originating in the Adirondack Mountains, the river stretches approximately 315 miles long, with its mouth starting in the New York Harbor and ending in the Atlantic Ocean. It also served as a source for drinking water to millions of New York residents. If your friend sells the house without your permission, you may still owe the full amount of the mortgage. To balance your 401k, review the available funds and determine an allocation based on your risk tolerance and total retirement fund (including IRAs). Aim for a mix that includes bonds, stocks, international investments, REIT, etc. You can adjust your allocations through your benefits/401k website, usually within one business day. Plan to rebalance your portfolio every year or after major life events. However, changes to new and match money may take place with the next paycheck.

401(k) contributions are pre-tax dollars which means you do not pay income tax on the contribution amount in the year you make the contribution. The funds then grow tax-deferred until retirement. When you withdraw funds from your 401(k) after retirement, the withdrawals are subject to income tax. The withdrawals are included as ordinary income on your tax return and taxed at your marginal tax rate in the year of the withdrawal. However, there is a 10% early withdrawal penalty if you withdraw funds before age 59 1/2, unless certain exceptions apply. It is also worth noting that if you have a Roth 401(k), contributions are made after-tax and qualified withdrawals are tax-free.

IRA stands for Individual Retirement Account. It's a personal savings account with tax advantages allowing you to save and invest for retirement. There are several types of IRAs, including Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs and SEP IRAs. Each has its own advantages and rules regarding contributions, distributions, and taxes. The key common point is that they're set up specifically for retirement savings, as opposed to regular brokerage or savings accounts. In an IRA, contributions grow tax-deferred, and in some cases, can be tax-deductible as well.

If your financial situation changes, it's a good idea to review your contribution amount and make adjustments accordingly.

To compare metrics for different periods, you can use the time period control to select the periods you want to view. The data points on the graph will adjust to an appropriate measurement period. 1. CPU Usage Alert: Triggers an alert when the CPU usage on a server exceeds a certain threshold, such as 90%, indicating potential performance issues that require attention.

Example condition: cpu\_usage > 90%

1. Memory Usage Alert: Monitors the memory usage on a server and sends an alert when it exceeds a specified threshold, helping you identify any potential performance problems caused by lack of memory.

Example condition: memory\_usage > 95%

1. Response Time Alert: Tracks the response time of an application and sends an alert if the response time exceeds a defined threshold, indicating a potential slowdown in application performance.

Example condition: response\_time > 5000ms

1. Disk Usage Alert: Monitors the disk usage on a server and alerts you when it reaches a specific threshold, helping you identify any potential storage performance bottlenecks and plan for increased storage capacity.

Example condition: disk\_usage > 80%

1. Concurrent User Alert: Monitors the number of concurrent users on an application and sends an alert when that number exceeds a defined threshold, helping you manage the load on your application servers and ensure good user experience.

Example condition: concurrent\_user > 500

1. Error Alert: Monitors the number of errors on an application and sends an alert when that number exceeds a certain threshold, helping you identify and troubleshoot issues that may be affecting the application's functionality.

Example condition: number\_of\_errors > 50 in the last hour

In the given document, weak understanding is a metric that represents the number of individual messages with weak understanding, which could indicate potential dialog problems. These messages are not classified by an intent and do not contain any known entities. By reviewing unrecognized messages, you can identify and address potential dialog problems or areas where the assistant's understanding may need improvement.

Yes, the conversations are monitored. In fact, the Watson Assistant Analytics dashboard allows you to view and analyze data from past interactions with the system. Here are some data points that are monitored:

* Intents: Displays the intent that Watson Assistant was most confident about detecting in each case.
* Entities: Presents information about user-defined entities or system entities recognized in users' messages.
* User inputs: Shows user input messages as they were received, regardless of how Watson Assistant interpreted them.
* Dialog nodes: Lists the dialog nodes that were triggered in each conversation and the number of times they were triggered.

Additionally, for privacy reasons, user data that is collected during conversations is anonymized and subject to legal and compliance requirements as specified in the IBM Trust Center. To learn more, you can check the documentation page for Analytics [here](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/watson-assistant?topic=watson-assistant-dialog-logs).
The billing for a Conversation service is based on the total number of API calls submitted during a billing cycle. The number of turns or per conversation does not impact the billing.

To filter messages in Watson Assistant, you can use various options such as Search user statements, Intents, Entities, and Time period.  - Search user statements: You can type a word or phrase in the search bar to filter messages based on user input. This method does not search the assistant's replies.  - Intents: Select the drop-down menu and type an intent in the input field, or choose from the populated list. You can select more than one intent to filter the results using any of the selected intents, including Irrelevant.  - Entities: Select the drop-down menu and type an entity name in the input field, or choose from the populated list. You can select more than one entity to filter the results by any of the selected entities. If you filter by intent and entity, your results will include the messages that have both values. You can also filter for results with No entities found.  - Time period: Select the drop-down menu and choose the desired time period, such as Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, or custom time range.  Note that it might take some time for messages to update, and you should allow at least 30 minutes after a user's interaction with your assistant before attempting to filter for that content.

In the wild, guinea pigs do not burrow or build nests themselves. Instead, they often seek shelter in the burrows of other animals, as well as in crevices and tunnels formed by vegetation. They are social animals that live in small groups, moving together while eating grass or other vegetation. Guinea pigs are most active during dawn and dusk, when it is harder for predators to spot them.

Guinea pigs are herbivores whose natural diet is grass. They have continuously growing molars suited for grinding plant matter. They may also eat their feces (coprophagy) as these include special soft pellets called cecotropes, which recycle vitamins, fiber, and bacteria required for proper digestion. Domesticated guinea pigs benefit from a diet of fresh grass hay, such as timothy or alfalfa hay, and food pellets which are often based on timothy hay. They also require fresh, raw fruits and vegetables to obtain enough vitamin C, as they cannot synthesize this vital nutrient on their own.

Cavia tschudii, also known as the montane guinea pig, is native to Peru and is adapted to a diet of grasses and other plant material like its domesticated counterpart. However, their specific eating habits and preferences may vary based on environmental factors such as seasonality and habitat.

Cavia tschudii, wild guinea pig, is preyed upon by a wide range of predators, including birds of prey, mammals such as foxes, and snakes. They also face pressure from habitat destruction caused by urbanization, agriculture, and deforestation. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has listed the wild guinea pig, Cavia tschudii, as a species of least concern due to its large range and adaptability to a wide variety of habitats.

Yes, that's true. Cuis, also known as cuyes or curíes, are a domesticated species of guinea pigs that have been reared for their meat in the Andean highlands of South America for thousands of years. They are a significant source of protein for many indigenous communities and have been traditionally reserved for ceremonial meals by these communities. In recent decades, cuy cuisine has gained popularity beyond indigenous communities and has become a common feature in restaurants in some South American countries.

In clinical research, a "human guinea pig" refers to a person who takes part in an experiment or trial. This term originates from the earlier practice of using guinea pigs in scientific experiments. The concept of a "human guinea pig" has been seen in various contexts, including literature, film, and activism. For instance, the book "100,000,000 Guinea Pigs" by F.J. Schlink and Arthur Kallet published in 1933, extended this metaphor to consumer society, and became a national bestseller in the United States, thereby further popularizing the term and contributing to the growth of the consumer protection movement. Additionally, during World War II, plastic surgeon Archibald McIndoe established the "Guinea Pig Club" at Queen Victoria Hospital in East Grinstead, Sussex, England for his patients who were undergoing previously untested reconstruction procedures, using the metaphor to describe his patients. The title "human guinea pig" is used in a literal sense when referring to individuals who agree to participate in medical experiments or drug trials.

Guinea pigs were a crucial part of vitamin C research in the early 20th century. From the accidental discovery in 1907 that scurvy could be induced in guinea pigs, to their use to prove the chemical structure of the 'ascorbutic factor' in 1932, the guinea pig model proved to be very useful in vitamin C research. This is because like humans, guinea pigs cannot synthesize their own vitamin C, and must obtain this vital nutrient from food. They require about 10 mg of vitamin C daily and if they do not ingest enough, they can suffer from potentially fatal scurvy. The discovery of the importance of vitamin C in guinea pigs led to its discovery and understanding as an essential nutrient for humans as well.

The CDC recommends maintaining a physical distance of at least 1.8 meters (6ft) between persons, washing hands often, and wearing a face mask to prevent the spread of the virus. A person can also be infected by touching a surface or object that has the virus on it and then touching their own mouth, nose, or eyes. It is recommended to avoid large gatherings, maintain good ventilation, and practice good hand and respiratory hygiene to reduce the risk of infection.

Some of the common side effects are pain and swelling on the arm where the person got the shot, as well as fever, chills, tiredness, and headache. COVID-19 vaccines work by teaching your immune system how to recognize and fight off the virus that causes the COVID-19 disease. The mRNA vaccines, like the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines, teach your body how to make a harmless piece of the virus called the "spike protein" which triggers an immune response. Your immune system then will remember how to fight this spike protein if you are exposed to COVID-19. The Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca vaccines work by using a harmless virus to introduce a piece of the COVID-19 virus to your immune system, triggering a response.

Data encryption is the process of converting plaintext or easily readable data into a format that cannot be understood by unauthorized users. Data encryption provides security for data at rest or in transit, ensuring that only authorized parties can access the encrypted information. Once encrypted, data can only be accessed or understood using a decryption key, which is typically kept secret and securely stored. Encryption is an essential tool for data protection in information security and privacy, and it serves a critical role in secure communication over insecure networks such as the Internet.

IBM Cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a virtual network created from your IBM Cloud account resources. It provides a secure, isolated virtual network for cloud resources, allowing for fine-grained control over your virtual infrastructure and network traffic segmentation. VPC resources include instances, images, subnets, VPN gateways, security groups, and SSH keys. They are isolated from other networks yet are scalable and secure. VPC can be deployed within a single region but span across multiple zones within that region. It also provides private connectivity through subnets, as well as optional access to the public internet via public gateways or floating IP addresses. Security measures include data-at-rest encryption and customer-managed keys for additional control over data security.

There are three different types of clouds available: public, private, and hybrid.

1. A public cloud includes a shared set of resources that are provisioned to allow access to a company's resources. It is hosted in a multi-tenant environment on a virtual server, and it can be accessed from anywhere.
2. A private cloud includes resources that are provisioned to allow access to a company's resources. It is hosted on dedicated hardware, such as a bare metal server, and either onsite at the company's office (or across offices) or by a cloud provider. A private cloud can be accessed from anywhere.
3. A hybrid cloud includes resources that combine the aspects of both public and private clouds. It is hosted both onsite at a company's office (or across offices) and by a cloud provider. A hybrid cloud can be accessed from anywhere.

The IBM Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) offers several benefits:

- **Flexibility:** VPC allows you to define and control your network as you see fit, giving you the freedom to allocate IP addresses and address ranges as needed.

The scientific objectives of NASA's Deep Impact Extended Mission, also known as EPOXI, included two parts. The Deep Impact Extended Investigation (DIXI) aimed to fly by comet 103P/Hartley 2 and return images and data for scientific analysis. The Extrasolar Planet Observation and Characterization (EPOCh) investigation focused on observing nearby bright stars with known large planets to characterize their orbital behavior and search for other planets in those systems.

The goals of the Deep Impact mission were to rendezvous with comet 9P/Tempel 1 and launch a projectile into the comet nucleus. Observations were made of the ejecta, much of which represented pristine material from the interior of the comet, the crater formation process, the resulting crater, and outgassing from the nucleus, particularly the newly exposed surface. The scientific objectives of the mission are to: improve the knowledge of the physical characteristics of cometary nuclei and directly assess the interior of cometary nucleus; determine properties of the surface layers such as density, strength, porosity, and composition from the crater and its formation; study the relationship between the surface layers of a cometary nucleus and the possibly pristine materials of the interior by comparison of the interior of the crater with the surface before impact; and improve our understanding of the evolution of cometary nuclei, particularly their approach to dormancy, by comparing the interior and the surface. This project was selected as a Discovery class mission in July, 1999.

The Deep Impact spacecraft consists of a 370 kg cylindrical copper impactor attached to a 650 kg flyby bus. The spacecraft is a box-shaped honeycomb aluminum framework with a flat rectangular Whipple debris shield mounted on one side. The spacecraft has body-mounted high- and medium-resolution instruments, each consisting of an imaging camera and an infrared spectrometer to observe the ejected ice and dust. The medium resolution camera has a field of view of 0.587 degrees and a resolution of 7 m/pixel at 700 km distance and is used for navigation and context images. The high-resolution camera has a FOV of 0.118 degrees and a resolution of 1.4 m/pixel at 700 km. The infrared spectrometers cover the range from 1.05 to 4.8 micrometers. The flyby spacecraft measures approximately 3.2 m x 1.7 m x 2.3 m, is three-axis stabilized, and uses a blowdown hydrazine primary propulsion system. The communications are through a 1-meter diameter parabolic dish antenna mounted on a 2-axis gimbal or through a fixed low-gain antenna. The power is provided by a 7.2 square meter solar array and stored in a small NiH2 battery. The spacecraft has two redundant RAD750 computers with 309 MB each of memory for scientific data.

The Deep Impact mission aimed to rendezvous with comet 9P/Tempel 1 and launch a projectile into the comet nucleus in order to study the ejecta, crater formation process, the resulting crater, and outgassing from the nucleus. The mission's goals were to improve our understanding of cometary nuclei, their interior, surface layers, and evolution. The spacecraft consisted of a copper impactor and a flyby bus equipped with imaging cameras and infrared spectrometers. The mission was a success and provided valuable data about the composition and behavior of comets.

The bin for compost should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size. This is mentioned in the Step 1 of the four easy steps to composting at home from the Backyard Composting website of Madison County, NY.

According to the provided document from Madison County, NY, there are four easy steps for composting at home:

1. Pick Out a Bin: Make sure your bin is at least 3x3x3 feet in size. A sunny vs. shady spot will impact how fast your compost will dry out or hold water. A closed bin (like a tumbler) is the only way to ensure you will keep critters out but will also keep out microbes which are needed to break down your waste. If you use a closed bin make sure to add a shovel full of soil from the ground. Keep your bin somewhere convenient to use and access.
2. Gather Materials: Gather materials such as leaves, vegetable scraps, grass clippings, newspaper, cardboard, and coffee grounds. Leave out feces from cats and dogs, invasive plants, weed seeds, oil, fats, plastics or non-organic matter. Use three parts brown (like leaves and cardboard) to one part green (like vegetable scraps and grass clippings) is optimal but does not have to be exact.
3. Maintain: Layers some small sticks and twigs at the bottom to help with air and drainage when starting. From here, you should layer your browns and greens. You can imagine you are making a bowl for your greens to lay in the middle and then add more browns on top. Keep your compost at 40-60% water content. Turning helps a pile break down faster and makes sure oxygen is present.
4. Harvest and More: You will know when your compost is done when it has a earthy smell and looks like rich dark soil. If you do not fully turn the pile, your finished compost will be at the bottom of the pile. If you are running out of browns; shredded newspaper, paper towel and toilet paper rolls make good brown additions.

The temperature of compost is important for the decomposition rates and for destroying pathogens and weed seeds. Beneficial microorganisms in a compost pile require a certain temperature range for optimal activity, which is usually between 131 to 160 degrees Fahrenheit. Pile conditions within that range will promote rapid decomposition and destroy pathogens and weed seeds. Above that temperature range, beneficial microorganisms cannot survive. Below that range, decomposition will occur more slowly, and pathogens and weed seeds may remain in the final compost. Pile temperatures must remain at 131 degrees Fahrenheit or above for several days to meet standards for reducing pathogens. The exact amount of time depends on the method of composting. Controlling the oxygen, moisture, pile structure, and nutrient balance helps achieve the optimal temperature range in a compost pile.

To help keep recyclables dry and to keep recyclables from blowing out of the container, we recommend placing your heavier plastic/metal/glass recycling bin on top of your paper/cardboard recycling bin to weigh everything down and keep the paper dry.

After entering a storm drain, water typically flows into a large exit at the discharge point, often covered by a grating. This exit leads to a natural or man-made water body like a canal, river, lake, reservoir, sea, or ocean. Some drains may discharge into individual dry wells or interconnected dry well systems. Additionally, storm drains can also empty into man-made excavations called recharge basins or retention ponds.

A catchbasin is a structure, usually found at the low point of a site that collects and detains sediment-laden runoff before it is discharged into a storm drain. They are often used as a first-line pretreatment for other treatment practices, such as retention basins, by capturing large sediments and street litter from urban runoff before it enters the storm drainage pipes. They are commonly designed with a sump area below the outlet pipe level which is a reservoir for water and debris to help prevent the pipe from clogging.

Yes, the purpose of the catchbasin in a storm drain system is to capture large sediments and street litter from urban runoff before it enters the storm drainage pipes. The efficiency with which it performs this task depends on the design of the catchbasin and on routine maintenance to retain the storage available in the sump to capture sediment. While the catchbasin can help to reduce the amount of litter and debris that enters the storm drainage pipes, it may not be able to capture all of the litter and debris from the water from the streets, roads, and roofs, some of the debris which is smaller in size may pass through the catchbasin and eventually settle in the storm drainage pipes or be discharged into a body of water.

The water that enters a storm drain can be recycled and used for various purposes such as irrigation, gardening, cleaning, and dust control. However, it is important to note that stormwater runoff is often contaminated with various pollutants, such as oils, heavy metals, fertilizers, pesticides, and other substances that can make it unsuitable for direct use without proper treatment. Treating stormwater runoff for non-potable purposes is often more cost-effective than treating it for potable (drinking) water, and there are many technologies available for treating stormwater runoff, such as sand filters, bioretention cells, and constructed wetlands. However, the use of stormwater runoff for non-potable purposes is still subject to regulations and permitting requirements in many jurisdictions.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has established guidelines and regulations for stormwater management under the Clean Water Act, which includes provisions for sustainable storm drain construction and management.  EPA issued stormwater regulations for large cities in 1990 and for other communities in 1999 . The permits require local governments to operate stormwater management programs, covering both construction of new buildings and facilities, and maintenance of their existing municipal drainage networks. The EPA also provides technical assistance and guidance to local governments on best management practices (BMPs) for stormwater management, including using low-impact development strategies, such as green infrastructure, to reduce stormwater runoff and improve water quality. The National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit program addresses water pollution by regulating point sources and by setting wastewater standards for industry. The NPDES permit program regulates municipal pollution as well. As of 2020, EPA has set guidelines for construction site control, industrial site control, and municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) control. EPA also encourages the use of Green Infrastructure to manage stormwater pollution, as well as using it in urban planning and design.

Storm drain systems vary from place to place, but they all serve the same purpose: to collect and move rainwater away from streets and buildings to prevent flooding. In some areas, the storm drain system may be connected to the municipal sewer system, while in others it may be separate. In some countries, the storm drain system is designed to collect and treat stormwater before discharging it into local water bodies, while in others it may be discharged directly into rivers, lakes, or the ocean. Some cities have adapted the use of green infrastructure like bio-swales (vegetated ditches), green roofs, and permeable pavement to capture and treat stormwater runoff before it enters the drainage system. In some parts of the developed world, storm drain systems are designed to be part of the larger urban water cycle and are integrated with wastewater treatment plants. In some parts of the developing world, where infrastructure is not present, alternative systems like infiltration trenches or swales might be used to manage stormwater runoff. Some low-lying areas with frequent flooding may have pumping stations to actively remove water from the storm drain system during heavy rainfall events.

The people of ancient Mesopotamia built extensive networks of canals for irrigation which also served the purpose of draining their fields after heavy rainfall . The city of Ur located in modern day Iraq is believed to be the first example of urban drainage systems . The Indus Valley Civilization developed some of the first sophisticated urban drainage systems in the world . In the Minoan civilization , large centralized drainage systems were built to prevent flooding. Early stormwater management systems in China , India and the Middle East included the use of reed beds as a form of catchment area to filter pollutants from stormwater runoff. The Romans also designed streets with a raised median to divert rainwater towards the gutters and cunettes which drained the street . During the medieval period, many cities in Europe also had well-developed stormwater management systems in place . Storm drains that diverted water from the city center into nearby streams or rivers that would then carry it away from the area. The renaissance saw a renewed interest in urban planning and stormwater management , with some of the first European underground sewers being built in cities such as Paris and London . This helped to alleviate the problem of flooding and water pollution in urban areas .

The Great Wall of China was built using a variety of materials including stone, brick, tamped earth, wood, and other materials. During the Ming Dynasty, bricks were heavily used, along with materials such as tiles, lime, and stone. Bricks were favored due to their size and weight, which made them easier to work with and more durable than rammed earth. Stone was used for the foundation, inner and outer brims, and gateways of the wall. Before bricks, the wall was mainly built from rammed earth, stones, and wood.

The Great Wall of China, as measured directly, is approximately 21,196 kilometers (13,171 miles) long. However, its length has varied throughout history as it was extended and parts of it have deteriorated. It is often referred to as the "Long Wall of 10,000 Li" (万里长城), where "li" (里) is a traditional Chinese unit of length, roughly equivalent to 500 meters. Thus, 10,000 li would correspond to about 5,000 kilometers. But this measurement is an approximation, as the actual length has changed over time.

The main enemies of China who the Great Wall was built to defend against were nomadic invasions, particularly from the Mongols, Turks, and other steppe tribes. These nomads were highly skilled in using cavalry in warfare and used the vast steppes to their advantage, making it challenging for the agrarian Chinese to fight against them. The wall was built as a defensive structure to protect Chinese states and empires against raids and invasions from these nomadic groups. Over time, the wall was repeatedly built, rebuilt, and maintained by different dynasties, with the majority of the existing wall today being built during the Ming Dynasty (1368--1644).

Qin Shi Huang is known for unifying China and becoming the first emperor of the Qin Dynasty. After the unification of China, he standardized weights, lengths, and currency, as well as the mode of transportation system. The Great Wall of China was built during his reign by connecting and strengthening previous fortifications to protect his state from nomads from the north. Apart from that, He is known for promoting Confucianism and Legalism as well as implementing Legalist policies. Also, He used forced labor to build his tomb at Mount Li, which is famous for the Terracotta Army. Lastly, He had an obsessive desire for immortality and tried to find an elixir of life, which eventually led to his death.

Meng Tian was a Chinese military general and engineer who served Qin Shi Huangdi, the first emperor of China. In 215 BC, he was sent to drive out the Xiongnu nomads from the Ordos region and build walls to protect the northern border of the Qin empire. His work extended from the sea on the east to the Yanzhi Mountains in the south and north for over 10,000 li. Meng Tian introduced 30,000 settler families to colonize the newly conquered territories. However, some historians believe that the project was doomed to fail due to its attempt to enforce agriculture on a land more suited for herding.

Scammers use a variety of methods to defraud unsuspecting victims, and these scams continue to evolve and change over time. Some of the most common scams and frauds currently include:

1. Phishing scams, where scammers impersonate a reputable company and contact people via email or text message with the goal of obtaining personal information, such as passwords or credit card information.
2. Investment scams, where scammers promote fake investment opportunities with the promise of high returns, but ultimately don't deliver.
3. Romance scams, where scammers pose as a potential romantic partner and engage in a relationship with a victim, building trust and ultimately asking for money.
4. Tech support scams, where scammers pose as computer technicians and offer to fix non-existent problems with a victim's computer, often for a fee.
5. Work-from-home scams, where scammers offer the opportunity to work from home, but the job is fake and the scammer uses the victim's personal information for fraudulent purposes.
6. Lottery and sweepstakes scams, where scammers inform the victims that they have won a large sum of money, but must pay a fee or taxes before they can collect their winnings.

Another common scam involves scammers offering foreclosure prevention or refinance assistance to homeowners for a fee. They may claim to be affiliated with a government agency, such as the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Federal Housing Administration (FHA), and may use logos or seals to make their materials look official. In reality, they are not affiliated with these agencies and are not providing the promised assistance.

It is important to be aware that, in most cases, it is illegal to charge an upfront fee for mortgage modification services. If a company promises to modify or refinance your mortgage for a fee, it is likely a scam.

The Defense of Marriage Act, or DOMA, is a U.S. federal law enacted in 1996, which defined marriage for federal purposes as a union between one man and one woman. It allowed states to refuse recognition of same-sex marriages granted under other states' laws. Before Section 3 of the Act was struck down in 2013, DOMA barred same-sex married couples from being recognized as "spouses" for federal law purposes, thus preventing them from receiving federal marriage benefits. The act was introduced and passed with large, veto-proof majorities in Congress and signed into law by President Bill Clinton.

The origin of the custom of breaking a glass at Jewish weddings is unknown , although many reasons have been given . The primary reason is that joy must always be tempered . This is based on two accounts in the Talmud of rabbis who , upon seeing that their son 's wedding celebration was getting out of hand , broke a vessel -- in the second case a glass -- to calm things down . Another explanation is that it is a reminder that despite the joy , Jews still mourn the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem . Because of this , some recite the verses `` If I forget thee / O Jerusalem ... '' ( Ps. 137 : 5 ) at this point . Many other reasons have been given by traditional authorities .

All states in the United States of America , including the District of Columbia , allow same - sex marriages . Since June 26 , 2015, following the United States Supreme Court decision in Obergefell v. Hodges , state level bans on same - sex marriage have been ruled unconstitutional , ensuring same - sex couples the right to marry nationwide in the United States. Prior to Obergefell , eighteen individual states and the District of Columbia permitted same - sex marriage , while thirty - two states either prohibited same - sex marriage by statute or by constitutional amendment . The individual state decisions were primarily the result of judicial actions following the Supreme Court decision in United States v. Windsor , which invalidated part of the Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA), and state actions following the Supreme Court decisions in Baker v. Nelson and Hollingsworth v . Perry . Additionally , same - sex marriages began in Delaware on July 1 , 2013, in Minnesota and Rhode Island on August 1, 2013, and in New Mexico on December 19, 2013, due to court rulings.

The Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) allows for a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (LPR) to petition for their foreign-born spouse to obtain a green card (permanent residence) in the United States. The IBM Cloud® Internet Services (CIS) bot features include JavaScript detections. It uses Google’s Picasso fingerprinting technique to inject a small amount of JavaScript into client devices. Picasso results are factored into bot scores and help CIS classify traffic as automated or human. BotScoreSrc: Not Computed and a score of 0 are relevant to Picasso JavaScript Fingerprinting requests. These requests are exempt from being blocked by any firewall rules. The JavaScript is only injected in response to requests for HTML pages or page views, excluding AJAX calls. API and mobile app traffic is unaffected. CIS collects data from requests flowing through its network every day. With this data, powered by Cloudflare's machine learning and behavior analysis, CIS can identify likely bot activity and can provide you with information on how to allow or disallow specific bot traffic using Firewall Rules. Cloudflare Bot Management uses the following detection mechanisms, each producing their own scores, which are then combined to form a single score:

* Machine learning: A highly accurate bot identification machine learning model trained on trillions of requests with minimal impact to request processing speed
* Heuristics engine: Detects bots by screening requests through a set of simple rules that capture bots based on certain attibutes of the requests made.
* Behavioral analysis: Detects bots that have never been seen, calculating and analyzing normal visitor behavior over an extended period of time.
* Verified bots: A way to avoid accidental blocks of useful bots using several validators and a bots directory of unique good bot identities.
* JS fingerprinting: A challenge-response system with challenge injected into the webpage on Cloudflare’s edge and rendered in the background for validation.

A secret is a piece of sensitive information, such as an API key, password, or any type of credential used to access a confidential system. The external service can then understand who you are and whether you're authorized to interact with it. Secrets must be securely protected through their entire lifecycle. Examples of secrets include passwords of any type (database logins, OS accounts, functional IDs, and so on), API keys, long-lived authentication tokens (OAuth2, GitHub, IAM, and so on), SSH keys, encryption keys, and other private keys.

To protect your privacy, it is recommended to avoid sharing personally identifiable information such as your name, location or any other private data when adding keys to a service. When creating keys, ensure that the key name does not contain any personal information and the key does not expire if necessary. Key aliases and key rings can be used to describe keys, and every key must be placed in a key ring. If a key has to be rotated, setting a rotation policy at key creation time is recommended. If an instance policy exists to create rotation policies on keys by default, this policy can be overwritten at key creation time. Root keys used for wrap or unwrap operations should be set as non-extractable. Finally, avoid using personal data as metadata for keys and always protect your confidential data.

No, Richard III is not historically accurate. Shakespeare's portrayal of Richard III as a malevolent villain is heavily influenced by the Tudor propaganda that painted him as a hunchback with a withered arm who was responsible for numerous murders, including those of his nephews, the Princes in the Tower. In reality, the historical Richard III was a much more complex figure, and many of the accusations leveled against him by Shakespeare's sources have been called into question by modern historians. The physical deformities attributed to him are now believed to be exaggerations or outright fabrications, although he may have had some degree of scoliosis. The true cause of the disappearance of the Princes in the Tower remains a mystery, and there is no concrete evidence linking Richard III to their deaths.

Meanwhile, Benjamin Graham, also known as the "father of value investing," coined the concept of "margin of safety" in investing. Peter Lynch emphasizes investing in what you know, Philip Fisher values long-term growth opportunities in companies, and Joel Greenblatt focuses on finding companies with high earnings yield and return on invested capital.

Benjamin Graham, widely regarded as the father of value investing, has inspired numerous successful investors, including Warren Buffett. The average return of Graham's investment strategy is difficult to quantify, as he focused on long-term value investing and was more concerned with the overall success of his approach than any specific returns.

As for Warren Buffett, his investment returns have averaged around 20% per year over his investing career, a record that few other investors can match. His strategy, which involves focusing on the long-term prospects of businesses rather than attempting to time the market, has proven to be a successful one. Keep in mind, that these returns are over a long period of time and not every year.

It is worth noting that while such a high average return is certainly impressive, it is important to remember that these returns are not guaranteed, and that past performance is not necessarily indicative of future results. It's also worth remembering that different investors have different goals and investment styles, and that what works for one investor may not work for another. The maximum amount you can contribute to a 401(k) plan is set by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and generally increases each year due to cost-of-living adjustments. For tax year 2023, the maximum amount an individual can contribute to a 401(k) plan is $20,500. If you are age 50 or over, you can make an additional catch-up contribution of up to $6,500, for a total of $27,000 in 2023. However, it's important to note that employer contributions also count toward the total limit. For example, if your employer contributes $10,000 to your 401(k) account, your maximum allowable contribution for the year would be reduced by that amount. Therefore, the total annual limit is the highest amount that can be added to your 401(k) account through both elective deferrals and employer contributions.

The limit on annual additions to your 401(k) account is determined by the Internal Revenue Code and is adjusted annually for inflation. These annual additions include employer contributions (i.e., matching and non-matching), your contributions as an employee and any forfeitures allocated to your account.

The annual additions paid to a participant's account cannot exceed the lesser of (a) 100% of the participant's compensation, or $54,000 ($60,000 including catch-up contributions) for 2017; $53,000 ($59,000 including catch-up contributions) for 2016. So, as long as the total contributions stay below that limit, you can contribute and accumulate as much as you want in your 401(k) account. It is important to check the 401(k) plan document for any additional limits.

In the event of a divorce, the division of assets, including retirement accounts like a 401(k), will be determined by the court. An early withdrawal from a 401(k) for purposes other than retirement is generally not advisable, as it can result in taxes and penalties. If you need the funds for a legitimate reason, such as paying off high-interest debt or avoiding foreclosure on your home, an early withdrawal may make sense, but it's essential to carefully weigh the potential consequences before making a decision. You should consult a financial advisor or a lawyer to assist you in your specific situation.

Alameda County's Mandatory Recycling Ordinance requires businesses, institutions, and multi-family properties in Alameda County to participate in recycling programs. Under the Ordinance, these organizations must provide their employees and tenants with adequate access to recycling services. To comply with the Ordinance, businesses and institutions must also source separate at least 3 types of recyclables (paper, cardboard, and bottles/cans) from their garbage, and multi-family properties of 5 or more units must provide on-site recycling services to their tenants.
Failure to comply with the Ordinance may result in a Notice of Violation and an administrative citation and fine for each offense. The fine amount is currently set at $500 for the first offense, $1,000 for the second offense, and $2,000 for each subsequent offense within a twelve-month period.
If your business or property is unable to comply with the Ordinance for any reason, you may apply for an exemption from the recycling requirements. To apply for an exemption, you must submit a written request to StopWaste, the agency responsible for enforcing the Ordinance, and provide supporting documentation as to why you are unable to comply. All exemption requests must be reviewed and approved by StopWaste before they are granted.

Vulnerability Advisor checks the security status of container images that are provided by IBM, third parties, or added to your organization's IBM Cloud Container Registry namespace. When you add an image to a namespace, it is automatically scanned by Vulnerability Advisor to detect security issues and potential vulnerabilities. If security issues are found, instructions are provided to help fix the reported vulnerability. Vulnerability Advisor generates a security status report that includes suggested fixes and best practices. It is available in two versions: version 3 and version 4. Vulnerability Advisor version 3 is deprecated from June 19, 2023. For more information about how to update to version 4, see [Update Vulnerability Advisor to version 4 by June 19, 2023](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/Registry?topic=Registry-registry_notices_va_v4&interface=ui). You can use IBM Cloud Security and Compliance Center to monitor vulnerabilities that are detected by Vulnerability Advisor. For more information, see [Getting started with Security and Compliance Center](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/security-compliance?topic=security-compliance-getting-started). Using Portieris to block the deployment of images with issues that are found by Vulnerability Advisor is deprecated.

If you are currently using Vulnerability Advisor version 3, it will continue to function until the end of support date, which is not available yet. However, from 19 June 2023, Vulnerability Advisor version 4 will be the default, and any Container Registry CLI commands that access version 3 will cease to work once it reaches its end of support date.

To continue using Vulnerability Advisor after version 3's end of support date, you will need to upgrade to version 4. There are different steps to take depending on whether you use IBM Cloud console, IBM Cloud CLI, Vulnerability Advisor REST API, or Vulnerability Advisor SDKs.

If you use IBM Cloud console to access Vulnerability Advisor, no action is required as it will be automatically updated to version 4.

If you use IBM Cloud CLI and want to use version 4 as the default, you must update the Container Registry CLI plug-in to version 1.0.0 or later, and run the command ibmcloud cr va-version-set v4.

If you use the Vulnerability Advisor REST API, you must update your client call from /va/api/v3 APIs to /va/api/v4 APIs.

If you use any of the Vulnerability Advisor version 3 SDKs to access Vulnerability Advisor, you must update to the Vulnerability Advisor version 4 SDK.

Exemptions that you previously defined continue to work, but the security notice value that comes back in Vulnerability Advisor version 4 might not be the same as for version 3. Therefore, if the returned value isn't the same as for version 3, you might have to update any existing exemptions that specify a security notice. Red Hat® security notices and exemptions that are defined by CVE value are unaffected.

Differences in Vulnerability Advisor version 4 behavior are documented in About Vulnerability Advisor.

Once updated to Vulnerability Advisor version 4, your security status will be automatically updated and any further vulnerabilities that may be found in images will be reported using the new version.

You can update to Vulnerability Advisor v4 by following the steps given in this documentation: [Update Vulnerability Advisor to version 4 by 19 June 2023](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/Registry?topic=Registry-registry_notices_va_v4&interface=ui)

For version 4, the image is indexed the first time that it is pushed. Thereafter, the vulnerability assessment is calculated every time Vulnerability Advisor is queried about that image.

IBM Cloud® Container Registry is a service for building and deploying applications in containers, and managing Docker images. Multiple user accounts and Docker clients can use the registry as a single source to manage the images. You can push your Docker images to the registry by using the `docker push` command. To control who can access the container images stored in IBM Cloud® Container Registry and what they can do, you can set policies for individual users or groups. The CIS (Center for Internet Security) Kubernetes Benchmark is a set of recommendations to configure Kubernetes securely and align with industry-specific security standards. When a new Kubernetes version is released, IBM engineers compare the default configuration of a cluster running that version against the benchmark and publish the results in their documentation. You can review how specific versions of your IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service or Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud clusters meet the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark.

The benchmark covers various areas such as master components, etcd, control plane configurations, worker nodes, and policies for users, network, and pod security. Each recommendation in the benchmark has a scoring system (scored or not scored), levels (Level 1 - practical measures or Level 2 - deeper measures), result status (Pass - compliant or Fail - non-compliant), and responsibilities (IBM, shared, or customer).

As a security administrator or auditor, you can use the benchmark to compare your company's internal standards and external regulatory requirements with the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark. The benchmark helps you to confirm basic security measures are in place and identify areas where you might enhance your security. The benchmark results are available for multiple versions, and you can access the documentation from the provided links.

The Berlin Wall began to fall on the evening of November 9, 1989. This followed several weeks of civil unrest, after which the East German government announced that its citizens could visit West Germany and West Berlin. People from both sides of the wall climbed onto it and chipped away parts in a celebratory atmosphere. The removal of the wall paved the way for German reunification, which formally took place on October 3, 1990.
The official reunification of Germany took place on 3 October 1990.

The number of people who died trying to cross the Berlin Wall, or as a result of the Wall's existence, has been disputed. Alexandra Hildebrandt, Director of the Checkpoint Charlie Museum and widow of the Museum's founder, estimated the death toll to be well above 200. A historic research group at the Center for Contemporary Historical Research (ZZF) in Potsdam has confirmed at least 140 deaths. Prior official figures listed 98 as being killed.

Early successful escapes involved people jumping the initial barbed wire or leaping out of apartment windows along the line. As the Wall was fortified, East German authorities no longer permitted apartments near the Wall to be occupied, and any building near the Wall had its windows boarded and later bricked up. Conrad Schumann was the first East German border guard to escape by jumping the barbed wire to West Berlin on 15 August 1961. Later, tunnels, hot air balloons, and even a self-made airplane were used to escape.

Most government agencies moved to Berlin, making it the capital, but many still maintain sizable presences in Bonn. The process took until 1999 to complete, when the Bundestag held its first session at the reconstructed Reichstag building in Berlin. Some government departments still maintain a presence in Bonn as of 2008.
The longtime leader of East Germany , Erich Honecker , resigned on 18 October 1989 and was replaced by Egon Krenz that day. Krenz was head of state when the Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989.
